nodes.title: An elementary bound for u cosh u − sinh u
nodes.statement: For every real u > 0: 0 < u cosh u − sinh u ≤ u³ cosh u / 2.
proofSteps: Positivity: u cosh u − sinh u = Σ_{j≥1} 2j u^{2j+1}/(2j + 1)! > 0.
Cauchy's mean value theorem (`exists_ratio_hasDerivAt_eq_ratio_slope`) for g(u) = u cosh u − sinh u and h(u) = u² on [0, u]: (u cosh u − sinh u)/u² = g′(v)/h′(v) = sinh v/2 for some v ∈ (0, u).
By the mean value theorem sinh v = v cosh w for some w ∈ (0, v), and cosh is increasing on [0, ∞): sinh v ≤ v cosh v ≤ u cosh u.

nodes.title: The termwise bound for the Rademacher series

Hence |R_k(n)| ≤ k·√k·u³ cosh u/(4√2πλ_n³) = α(n)³ cosh(α(n)/k)/(4√2πλ_n³k^{3/2}), and α(n)³/λ_n³ = π³(2/3)^{3/2} gives the constant π²/(6√3).

nodes.title: An effective bound for the remainder of the Rademacher series
hypotheses: n ≥ 1, N ≥ 1. The bound uses only the trivial estimate |A_k(n)| ≤ k; Rademacher's sharper bound (7) quoted by Lehmer 1939 has the same shape.
proofSteps: p(n) − Σ_{k≤N} R_k(n) = Σ_{k>N} R_k(n) (rademacher-exact-formula).
For k ≥ N + 1, cosh(α(n)/k) ≤ cosh(α(n)/(N + 1)) (cosh increasing on [0, ∞)), so Σ_{k>N}|R_k(n)| ≤ (π²/(6√3)) cosh(α(n)/(N + 1)) Σ_{k>N} k^{−3/2} (rademacher-term-bound).
Σ_{k>N} k^{−3/2} ≤ ∫_N^∞ x^{−3/2} dx = 2N^{−1/2} (`AntitoneOn.sum_le_integral` on [N, N + M] and M → ∞).

nodes.title: Explicit error of the truncated Hardy–Ramanujan sum
nodes.statement: For n ≥ 1 and N ≥ 1 let φ_k(n) = (√k/(2π√2))·d/dm(e^{α(m)/k}/λ_m) at m = n, i.e. φ_k(n) = √k·e^{u}(u − 1)/(4√2πλ_n³) with u = α(n)/k. Then |p(n) − Σ_{k=1}^{N} A_k(n)φ_k(n)| ≤ (π²/(3√3))·N^{−1/2}·cosh(α(n)/(N + 1)) + N^{5/2}/(4√2π·λ_n³).
hypotheses: n ≥ 1, N ≥ 1; A_k(n) is real.
proofSteps: R_k(n) − A_k(n)φ_k(n) = A_k(n)√k(u + 1)e^{−u}/(4√2πλ_n³) with u = α(n)/k, from u cosh u − sinh u = ((u − 1)e^u + (u + 1)e^{−u})/2 (rademacher-term).

nodes.title: Wirtinger derivatives ∂/∂τ and ∂/∂τ̄
nodes.statement: For F : ℂ → ℂ and z ∈ ℂ put ∂F(z) := ½(DF(z)(1) − i·DF(z)(i)) and ∂̄F(z) := ½(DF(z)(1) + i·DF(z)(i)), where DF(z) = fderiv ℝ F z is the real Fréchet derivative (junk value 0 where F is not real-differentiable). In coordinates z = u + iv these are ½(∂_u − i∂_v) and ½(∂_u + i∂_v). A function f : ℍ → ℂ is differentiated through F = f ∘ ofComplex (which agrees with f on the open set {Im z > 0}); we write ∂_τ f and ∂_τ̄ f for these, following the notation ∂/∂τ, ∂/∂τ̄ of Bruinier–Funke §3.
hypotheses: Two declarations defined together: Complex.wirtingerDeriv (∂) and Complex.wirtingerDerivBar (∂̄); the ℍ-versions are the compositions with UpperHalfPlane.ofComplex, not new definitions.
No holomorphy is assumed; for complex-differentiable F one has ∂F = F′ and ∂̄F = 0.
proofSteps: Define both as ℂ-combinations of fderiv ℝ F z applied to 1 and to i.

Cauchy–Riemann: DF(z) is ℂ-linear iff DF(z)(i) = i·DF(z)(1) iff ∂̄F(z) = 0; then ∂F(z) = DF(z)(1) = deriv F z (Mathlib's HasFDerivAt.restrictScalars direction and the converse by constructing the ℂ-linear map).
Leibniz and conjugation rules: fderiv ℝ of a product and of conj ∘ F, then collect terms.

Laplacian compatibility: expand ∂∂̄ = ¼(∂_u² + ∂_v²) and compare with InnerProductSpace.laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_complexPlane (iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 F z ![1,1] + ![I,I]) for C² functions (symmetry of second derivatives).
acceptance: 4∂∂̄F equals Mathlib's Laplacian of F for every C² function F : ℂ → ℂ.

nodes.title: The weight-k hyperbolic Laplacian Δ_k
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℝ and f : ℍ → ℂ, Δ_k f(τ) := −v²(∂²_u + ∂²_v)f(τ) + ikv(∂_u + i∂_v)f(τ) = −4v²∂_τ∂_τ̄ f(τ) + 2ikv ∂_τ̄ f(τ), where τ = u + iv (Bruinier–Funke (3.1); Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (2.1)). Real weight is admitted so that the same operator serves the integral weights of QM.3 and the weight 1/2 of QM.4. Zwegers' weight-1/2 Casimir operator Ω_{1/2} = −4v²∂_τ∂_τ̄ + iv∂_τ̄ + 3/16 equals Δ_{1/2} + 3/16, so 'eigenfunction of Ω_{1/2} with eigenvalue 3/16' means 'annihilated by Δ_{1/2}'.
hypotheses: k ∈ ℝ; f is differentiated through f ∘ ofComplex; the value is only meaningful where f is C².
Sign convention pinned: the first-order term is +ikv(∂_u + i∂_v) = 2ikv∂_τ̄, so holomorphic functions are annihilated for every k.
proofSteps: Define Δ_k f(τ) := −4 (Im τ)² ∂(∂̄(f ∘ ofComplex))(τ) + 2ik (Im τ) ∂̄(f ∘ ofComplex)(τ).
The coordinate form follows from ∂∂̄ = ¼(∂_u² + ∂_v²) and 2∂̄ = ∂_u + i∂_v (QM.3/wirtinger-derivatives).
Δ_k(v^s) = s(1 − k − s)v^s: ∂̄v^s = (is/2)v^{s−1}, ∂∂̄v^s = ¼s(s−1)v^{s−2}; substitute.
The Casimir identity is the case k = 1/2: 2·(1/2)·i v ∂̄ = iv∂̄.
acceptance: Δ_k(1) = 0 and Δ_k(v^{1−k}) = 0 (the two harmonic functions of the constant Fourier term, BF p. 9).
Δ_0 = −v²·Δ with Mathlib's Laplacian Δ.
Δ_k(τ̄) = 2ikv ≠ 0 for k ≠ 0, so the sign of the first-order term is detected.

nodes.title: Factorisation of Δ_k through raising and lowering
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℝ and f : ℍ → ℂ of class C²: −Δ_k f = L_{k+2}R_k f + k f = R_{k−2}L_k f (Bruinier–Funke (3.3), Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (2.2)).
hypotheses: f of class C² on ℍ (as f ∘ ofComplex on {Im > 0}).
proofSteps: Symmetry ∂∂̄ = ∂̄∂ on C² functions (Mathlib's symmetry of second derivatives).
acceptance: Applied to f = v^{1−k}: L_k v^{1−k} = (1−k)v^{2−k}, R_{k−2}((1−k)v^{2−k}) = 0 (R_w kills v^{−w}), consistent with Δ_k v^{1−k} = 0.

sources.match: Exactly the statement.

nodes.title: Raising and lowering shift Δ-eigenvalues
nodes.statement: If f : ℍ → ℂ is of class C³ and Δ_k f = λf, then Δ_{k+2}(R_k f) = (λ + k)R_k f and Δ_{k−2}(L_k f) = (λ − k + 2)L_k f (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (2.3), (2.4)).
hypotheses: k ∈ ℝ, λ ∈ ℂ, f of class C³ (so that R_k f, L_k f are C²).
proofSteps: From QM.3/laplacian-raising-lowering-factorisation at weight k + 2: −Δ_{k+2}R_k f = R_k L_{k+2} R_k f = R_k(−Δ_k f − kf) = −(λ + k)R_k f.
At weight k − 2: −Δ_{k−2}L_k f = L_k R_{k−2} L_k f + (k−2)L_k f = L_k(−Δ_k f) + (k − 2)L_k f = −(λ − k + 2)L_k f.
acceptance: For harmonic f of weight 2 − k (λ = 0) iterating gives Δ_{k−2}R^{k−2}_{2−k}f = (2 − k)R^{k−2}_{2−k}f, the step used in the proof of BOR Theorem 1.1.

sources.match: Exactly the statement.

nodes.title: The ξ-operator ξ_k (shadow operator)
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℝ and f : ℍ → ℂ, ξ_k f(τ) := 2i v^k \overline{∂_τ̄ f(τ)} = v^{k−2} \overline{L_k f(τ)} = R_{−k}(v^k \overline{f})(τ) (Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.2; Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (1.1)). It is conjugate-linear, kills exactly the holomorphic functions, and maps weight k to weight 2 − k. For a harmonic Maass form f, ξ_k f is its shadow (up to the convention of complex conjugation of coefficients made explicit in QM.3/xi-fourier-expansion).
hypotheses: k ∈ ℝ; v^k is the real power (Im τ)^k.
ξ_k is ℝ-linear and conjugate-linear over ℂ: ξ_k(cf) = c̄ ξ_k f.
proofSteps: Define ξ_k f(τ) := 2i (Im τ)^k conj(∂̄(f ∘ ofComplex)(τ)).
v^{k−2}\overline{L_k f} = v^{k−2}\overline{−2iv²∂̄f} = 2iv^k\overline{∂̄f}.
R_{−k}(v^k f̄) = 2i∂(v^k f̄) − kv^{k−1}f̄ = 2iv^k\overline{∂̄f} + 2ikv^{k−1}(∂v)f̄ − kv^{k−1}f̄ = 2iv^k\overline{∂̄f} (∂v = −i/2).
acceptance: For n < 0: ξ_k(Γ(1−k, 4π|n|v)e(nτ)) = −(4π|n|)^{1−k}e(|n|τ), the normalisation of Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (1.3).

nodes.title: ξ_{2−k} ∘ ξ_k = −Δ_k
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℝ and f : ℍ → ℂ of class C²: ξ_{2−k}(ξ_k f) = −Δ_k f.
hypotheses: f of class C² on ℍ.
proofSteps: Put h = L_k f, so ξ_k f = v^{k−2}h̄. Compute L_{2−k}(v^{k−2}h̄) = −2iv²∂̄(v^{k−2}h̄) = (k−2)v^{k−1}h̄ − 2iv^k\overline{∂h} (∂̄v = i/2, ∂̄h̄ = \overline{∂h}).
Conjugating: \overline{L_{2−k}(ξ_k f)} = v^k(2i∂h + (k−2)v^{−1}h) = v^k R_{k−2}h.
ξ_{2−k}(ξ_k f) = v^{−k}\overline{L_{2−k}ξ_k f} = R_{k−2}L_k f = −Δ_k f by QM.3/laplacian-raising-lowering-factorisation.
acceptance: For f = v^{1−k}: ξ_k f = 1 − k (constant), ξ_{2−k}(1 − k) = 0 = −Δ_k v^{1−k}.

sources.match: With ξ_k f = v^{k−2}\overline{L_k f} (Prop. 3.2) this identity gives ξ_{2−k}ξ_k = R_{k−2}L_k = −Δ_k, the form in which BF use it (Prop. 3.2, Thm. 3.7).

nodes.title: ξ_k f is holomorphic iff Δ_k f = 0
nodes.statement: Let U ⊆ ℍ be open, k ∈ ℝ and f of class C² on U. Then ξ_k f is holomorphic on U if and only if Δ_k f = 0 on U. Pointwise: ∂_τ(v^k ∂_τ̄ f) = −¼ v^{k−2} Δ_k f.
hypotheses: f of class C² on the open set U (ξ_k f is then C¹, so holomorphy is ∂̄(ξ_k f) = 0).
proofSteps: ∂̄(ξ_k f) = ∂̄(2iv^k\overline{∂̄f}) = 2i·\overline{∂(v^k∂̄f)} (v real), which vanishes iff ∂(v^k∂̄f) = 0 iff Δ_k f = 0.
Holomorphy of a C¹ function is ∂̄ = 0 (QM.3/wirtinger-derivatives, characterisation API).
acceptance: Δ_k(τ̄) = 2ikv ≠ 0 and ξ_k(τ̄) = 2iv^k is not holomorphic for k ≠ 0, consistent with the lemma.
This replaces the Fourier-coefficient argument of Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.2 (via Lemma 3.1) by a pointwise identity, so it holds on any open set.

sources.match: The holomorphy half of Prop. 3.2; proved here pointwise instead of through Lemma 3.1.

nodes.title: R_k and L_k intertwine the slash actions
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℤ, γ ∈ GL₂(ℝ) with det γ = 1 and f : ℍ → ℂ real-differentiable: R_k(f|_kγ) = (R_k f)|_{k+2}γ and L_k(f|_kγ) = (L_k f)|_{k−2}γ, where |_k is Mathlib's weight-k slash action (f|_kγ)(τ) = (cτ + d)^{−k}f(γτ).
hypotheses: det γ = 1 (for det γ > 0 Mathlib's slash carries the extra factor det(γ)^{k−1}, which changes the statement by a scalar).
proofSteps: Chain rule for ∂, ∂̄ along the holomorphic map τ ↦ γτ: ∂(F∘γ) = (∂F∘γ)·γ′, ∂̄(F∘γ) = (∂̄F∘γ)·\overline{γ′}, γ′(τ) = (cτ+d)^{−2}.
R_k(f|_kγ) − (R_kf)|_{k+2}γ = (cτ+d)^{−k−1}f(γτ)·[−2ikc + (k/v)(cτ+d) − (k/v)(cτ̄+d)] = (cτ+d)^{−k−1}f(γτ)·[−2ikc + (k/v)·c·2iv] = 0, using ∂(cτ+d)^{−k} = −kc(cτ+d)^{−k−1} and 1/Im(γτ) = |cτ+d|²/v.
For L_k only ∂̄ of the holomorphic factor (cτ+d)^{−k} vanishes; v² transforms by |cτ+d|^{−4}, giving weight k − 2.
acceptance: For γ = T (translation) both identities reduce to translation invariance; for γ = S they are the classical S-covariance.

sources.match: Exactly the statement (Mathlib's slash with det γ = 1 is the source's (6.2)).

nodes.title: Δ_k commutes with the weight-k slash action
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℤ, γ ∈ GL₂(ℝ) with det γ = 1 and f of class C² on ℍ: Δ_k(f|_kγ) = (Δ_k f)|_kγ. In particular the Δ_k-harmonic functions of weight k form a space stable under the slash action.
hypotheses: det γ = 1.
proofSteps: −Δ_k = R_{k−2}L_k (QM.3/laplacian-raising-lowering-factorisation).
Apply QM.3/raising-lowering-slash-equivariance twice: R_{k−2}L_k(f|_kγ) = R_{k−2}((L_kf)|_{k−2}γ) = (R_{k−2}L_kf)|_kγ.
acceptance: If f is harmonic of weight k then so is f|_kγ; used for the Maass–Poincaré series (termwise harmonicity).

sources.match: Equivariance of R_k, L_k; combined with (3.3) it gives the equivariance of Δ_k.

nodes.title: ξ_k intertwines weight k and weight 2 − k
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℤ, γ ∈ GL₂(ℝ) with det γ = 1 and f real-differentiable on ℍ: ξ_k(f|_kγ) = (ξ_k f)|_{2−k}γ.
hypotheses: det γ = 1.
proofSteps: ξ_k(f|_kγ)(τ) = 2iv^k\overline{∂̄[(cτ+d)^{−k}f(γτ)]} = 2iv^k(cτ̄+d)^{−k}(cτ+d)^{−2}\overline{(∂̄f)(γτ)} (chain rule, ∂̄ of the holomorphic factor vanishes).
(ξ_kf)|_{2−k}γ(τ) = (cτ+d)^{k−2}·2i(v/|cτ+d|²)^k\overline{(∂̄f)(γτ)} = 2iv^k(cτ+d)^{−2}(cτ̄+d)^{−k}\overline{(∂̄f)(γτ)}; the two agree.
acceptance: If f is Γ-invariant of weight k then ξ_k f is Γ-invariant of weight 2 − k (the transformation half of BF Prop. 3.2).

sources.match: The transformation behaviour asserted there, stated for a single γ.

nodes.title: Iterated raising operator R^n_k
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℝ, n ∈ ℕ: R^0_k := id and R^{n+1}_k := R_{k+2n} ∘ R^n_k, so R^n_k = R_{k+2(n−1)} ∘ ⋯ ∘ R_{k+2} ∘ R_k maps weight k to weight k + 2n (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades p. 7). Closed form (Lewis–Zagier (4.15), with ∂_h := D − h/(2πv) = −(4π)^{−1}R_{2h}): R^n_k = (−4π)^n Σ_{m=0}^{n} n!/(n−m)! · binom(n + k − 1, m) · (−1/(4πv))^m D^{n−m}, D = (2πi)^{−1}∂_τ.
hypotheses: k ∈ ℝ, n ∈ ℕ; f of class C^n; binom(x, m) is the generalised binomial coefficient for real x.
proofSteps: Define by recursion on n.
Closed form by induction on n using D(v^{−m}) = m v^{−m−1}/(4π) (Lewis–Zagier's (4.15), rewritten through R_w = −4π(D − w/(4πv))).
acceptance: R^1_k = R_k and R^2_0 e(τ) = (16π² − 8π/v)e(τ).
In the closed form, the specialisation n = k − 1 in weight 2 − k kills all terms with m ≥ 1 (Bol's identity).

nodes.title: Bol's identity D^{k−1} = (−4π)^{1−k}R^{k−1}_{2−k}
nodes.statement: For an integer k ≥ 2 and f : ℍ → ℂ of class C^{k−1}: D^{k−1}f = (−4π)^{1−k} R^{k−1}_{2−k} f, where D = (2πi)^{−1}∂_τ. Consequently, for k ∈ ℤ and det γ = 1, D^{k−1}(f|_{2−k}γ) = (D^{k−1}f)|_kγ.
proofSteps: Specialise QM.3/iterated-raising-operator's closed form to n = k − 1, weight 2 − k: binom(n + (2−k) − 1, m) = binom(0, m) = 0 for m ≥ 1, leaving (−4π)^{k−1}D^{k−1}.
The equivariance follows from iteratedRaising_slash.
acceptance: Lewis–Zagier's remark: in the case n + 2h = 1 the operators ∂^n_h and D^n agree (their (4.14)–(4.15)).

nodes.title: The upper incomplete gamma function Γ(s, x)
nodes.statement: For s ∈ ℝ and x > 0, Γ(s, x) := ∫_x^∞ t^{s−1}e^{−t} dt (DLMF 8.2.2); the integral converges for every real s because x > 0. Totalised by Γ(s, x) := 0 for x ≤ 0. For s > 0: Γ(s, x) + γ(s, x) = Γ(s), with Tau Ceti's lower incomplete gamma γ(s, x) = TauCeti.lowerIncompleteGamma s x.
hypotheses: Real parameter s (every real value, including s ≤ 0), real argument x > 0. The complex and branch-cut continuations of DLMF 8.2 are not needed.
proofSteps: Define as the Bochner integral over (x, ∞) of t^{s−1}e^{−t} (integrable: t^{s−1}e^{−t} ≤ C e^{−t/2} on [x, ∞)).
Γ(s,x) + γ(s,x) = Γ(s) for s > 0: split ∫_0^∞ at x (Real.Gamma_eq_integral, TauCeti.lowerIncompleteGamma_eq_integral).
Recurrence Γ(s+1, x) = sΓ(s, x) + x^s e^{−x}: integrate by parts on [x, ∞) (DLMF 8.8.2).
d/dx Γ(s, x) = −x^{s−1}e^{−x} for x > 0 (fundamental theorem of calculus).
Γ(n+1, x) = n! e^{−x}Σ_{j≤n}x^j/j! by the recurrence and Γ(1, x) = e^{−x} (DLMF 8.4.8, 8.4.5).
Γ(1/2, x²) = √π erfc(x) for x > 0: substitute t = u² (DLMF 8.4.6) and compare with TauCeti.Real.erfc.
Γ(s, x) ~ x^{s−1}e^{−x} as x → ∞ (DLMF 8.11.2, first term): l'Hôpital with the derivative formula.
acceptance: The function is defined at s = 0 (Γ(0, x) = E₁(x)), where the complete Gamma function has a pole.

nodes.title: The decaying non-holomorphic Fourier basis functions
nodes.statement: Let w ∈ ℝ, h > 0 and n ∈ ℤ with n < 0, and put φ_n(τ) := Γ(1 − w, 4π|n|v/h)·e(nτ/h). Then Δ_w φ_n = 0, ξ_w φ_n = −(4π|n|/h)^{1−w}·e(|n|τ/h), L_w φ_n(τ) = −v^{2−w}(4π|n|/h)^{1−w}e(nτ̄/h), and φ_n(τ) = O(v^{−w}e^{−2π|n|v/h}) as v → ∞. Also Δ_w(v^{1−w}) = 0 and ξ_w(v^{1−w}) = 1 − w.
hypotheses: w ∈ ℝ arbitrary; n < 0; h > 0 (the cusp width).
proofSteps: Write φ_n = b(v)e(nu/h) with b(v) = Γ(1−w, cv)e^{cv/2}, c = 4π|n|/h; use d/dx Γ(1−w, x) = −x^{−w}e^{−x} (QM.3/upper-incomplete-gamma).

With c = 4π|n|/h one has e(nτ/h) = e^{2πinu/h}e^{cv/2}; since 2πin/h + ic/2 = 0 for n < 0, the terms without a derivative of Γ cancel and ∂̄φ_n = −(i/2)c(cv)^{−w}e^{−cv/2}e^{2πinu/h} = −(i/2)c^{1−w}v^{−w}e(nτ̄/h).
ξ_w φ_n = 2iv^w\overline{∂̄φ_n} = −c^{1−w}e(−nτ/h) = −(4π|n|/h)^{1−w}e(|n|τ/h); holomorphic, hence Δ_w φ_n = 0 by QM.3/xi-holomorphic-iff-harmonic; L_w φ_n = −2iv²∂̄φ_n gives the stated formula.
Growth: Γ(1−w, x) = O(x^{−w}e^{−x}) (QM.3/upper-incomplete-gamma asymptotic) and |e(nτ/h)| = e^{2π|n|v/h}.
acceptance: For h = 1 and w = 2 − k this is the term c^−(n)Γ(k−1, 4π|n|y)q^n of Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (1.2), and the ξ formula is their (1.3).

sources.match: For w < 0 (index n < 0) H(2πnv)e(nu) = Γ(1−k, 4π|n|v)e(nτ); the lemma checks that it solves the equation.
The ξ-image of a single basis function, with w = 2 − k, h = 1.

nodes.title: The growing non-holomorphic Fourier basis functions
nodes.statement: Let w ∈ ℝ, h > 0, n ∈ ℤ with n > 0, W := 2πnv/h and ψ_n(τ) := e^{−W}(∫_1^W s^{−w}e^{2s}ds)·e(nu/h). Then Δ_w ψ_n = 0 and ξ_w ψ_n = (2πn/h)^{1−w}e(−nτ/h); e^{−W}∫_1^W s^{−w}e^{2s}ds ~ ½W^{−w}e^{W} as v → ∞ (the radial coefficient; ψ_n also carries the phase e(nu/h)). Every solution b of b″ − b + (w/W)(b′ + b) = 0 on W > 0 is a combination of e^{−W} and e^{−W}∫_1^W s^{−w}e^{2s}ds.
hypotheses: n > 0, h > 0, w ∈ ℝ. The base point 1 of the integral is a fixed normalisation; changing it adds a multiple of e^{−W}, i.e. of the holomorphic term e(nτ/h) (see sourceIssue E403).
proofSteps: Reduction of order: b = e^{−W}c turns the ODE into c″ + (w/W − 2)c′ = 0, so c′ = C W^{−w}e^{2W}.
∂̄[b(W)e(nu/h)] = (πin/h)(b + b′)(W) e(nu/h) and b + b′ = W^{−w}e^{W} for b = e^{−W}∫_1^W, so ∂̄ψ_n = (πin/h)W^{−w}e(nτ̄/h).
ξ_w ψ_n = 2iv^w\overline{∂̄ψ_n} = (2πn/h)v^w W^{−w} e(−nτ/h) = (2πn/h)^{1−w}e(−nτ/h); holomorphic, so Δ_w ψ_n = 0 (QM.3/xi-holomorphic-iff-harmonic).
Asymptotics: ∫_1^W s^{−w}e^{2s}ds ~ ½W^{−w}e^{2W} (l'Hôpital).
acceptance: The ξ-image of ψ_n is a negative power of q, so non-zero coefficients of ψ_n in f produce the principal part of ξ_w f.

sources.match: The ODE; for w > 0 the lemma supplies an explicit second solution.
The growth e^{W}W^{−w} of the second solution for W → +∞.

nodes.title: Exponential growth at the cusps
nodes.statement: For c ∈ ℙ¹(ℝ) = OnePoint ℝ, f : ℍ → ℂ and k ∈ ℤ: f has exponential growth at c in weight k if for every g ∈ GL₂(ℝ) with g·∞ = c there is C ∈ ℝ with (f|_kg)(τ) = O(e^{C·Im τ}) as Im τ → ∞ (uniformly in Re τ, i.e. along Mathlib's filter atImInfty). For a subgroup Γ ≤ GL₂(ℝ), f has exponential growth at the cusps of Γ if this holds at every c with IsCusp c Γ. This is condition (ii) of Bruinier–Funke §3 and the growth condition of weakly holomorphic forms; it is the analogue of Mathlib's OnePoint.IsBoundedAt with the bound 1 replaced by e^{C Im τ}.
hypotheses: Two declarations: OnePoint.IsExpGrowthAt c f k (one cusp) and IsExpGrowthAtCusps Γ f k (all cusps of Γ).
proofSteps: Define IsExpGrowthAt c f k :≡ ∀ g : GL₂(ℝ), g • ∞ = c → ∃ C, (f ∣[k] g) =O[atImInfty] (τ ↦ exp(C·Im τ)).
Bounded ⇒ exponential growth (take C = 0), from Mathlib's OnePoint.IsBoundedAt.

nodes.title: Weakly holomorphic modular forms M^!_k(Γ)
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ GL₂(ℝ) and k ∈ ℤ, a weakly holomorphic modular form of weight k for Γ is a function f : ℍ → ℂ that is holomorphic on ℍ, satisfies f|_kγ = f for all γ ∈ Γ, and has exponential growth at every cusp of Γ (QM.3/exponential-growth-at-cusps); equivalently (for arithmetic Γ) its expansion at every cusp has only finitely many negative powers of q (QM.3/weakly-holomorphic-laurent-expansion). The ℂ-vector space is M^!_k(Γ). It contains Mathlib's ModularForm Γ k (bounded at the cusps).
hypotheses: Γ : Subgroup (GL (Fin 2) ℝ); theorems about expansions assume Γ arithmetic (Subgroup.IsArithmetic) and, for linearity of the slash action over ℂ, Γ.HasDetOne.
Poles are allowed only at the cusps (the source's 'meromorphic at the cusps'), never in ℍ.
proofSteps: Structure extending SlashInvariantForm Γ k with fields holo' (MDifferentiable) and expGrowth' (IsExpGrowthAtCusps Γ k).
Module structure: pointwise operations; closure uses the API of exponential growth and of slash invariance.
Coercion from ModularForm Γ k: bounded at cusps ⇒ exponential growth (OnePoint.IsBoundedAt.isExpGrowthAt).
Products: M^!_k × M^!_l → M^!_{k+l} (slash of products for det = 1; growth adds).

1/Δ ∈ M^!_{−12}(SL₂(ℤ)): Δ = ModularForm.discriminant never vanishes on ℍ (ModularForm.discriminant_ne_zero), is invariant of weight 12, and e^{−2πv} = O(Δ) at ∞ (ModularForm.exp_isBigO_discriminant), so |1/Δ| = O(e^{2πv}).
Odd weight with −I ∈ Γ: f = f|_k(−I) = (−1)^k f forces f = 0.
acceptance: 1/Δ ∈ M^!_{−12}(SL₂(ℤ)) with expansion q^{−1} + 24 + O(q), not bounded at ∞.
j = E₄³/Δ ∈ M^!_0(SL₂(ℤ)); M_k(Γ) ⊆ M^!_k(Γ).

nodes.title: Laurent expansion of weakly holomorphic forms at a cusp
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ GL₂(ℝ) be arithmetic, f ∈ M^!_k(Γ) and h = Γ.strictWidthInfty > 0. Then there are N ∈ ℕ and a : ℤ → ℂ with a(n) = 0 for n < −N such that f(τ) = Σ_{n∈ℤ} a(n)e(nτ/h), absolutely and locally uniformly convergent on ℍ; a(n) = h^{−1}∫_0^h f(u + iv)e(−n(u+iv)/h)du for every v > 0. Conversely a holomorphic h-periodic function with such an expansion has exponential growth at ∞.
hypotheses: Γ arithmetic, so h > 0 and T^h ∈ Γ (Mathlib's strictPeriods).
proofSteps: f(τ + h) = f(τ) since T^h ∈ Γ; so f(τ) = F(e(τ/h)) with F holomorphic on the punctured unit disc (Mathlib's cuspFunction h f).
|F(q)| = O(|q|^{−C h/2π}) as q → 0 by exponential growth, so F has at most a pole at 0 (Riemann's removable singularity theorem applied to q^N F(q)).
The Laurent expansion of F gives the Fourier expansion; the coefficient formula is the Cauchy integral over |q| = e^{−2πv/h}.

sources.match: Meromorphy at the cusps (the definition used by BF) is the finite Laurent tail proved here from exponential growth.

nodes.title: Harmonic (weak) Maass forms H_k(Γ)
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ GL₂(ℝ) and k ∈ ℤ, a harmonic weak Maass form of weight k for Γ is a function f : ℍ → ℂ of class C² (as f ∘ ofComplex on {Im > 0}) such that (i) f|_kγ = f for all γ ∈ Γ, (ii) f has exponential growth at every cusp of Γ, (iii) Δ_k f = 0. The ℂ-vector space is H_k(Γ) (Bruinier–Funke's H_{k,L}(Γ″) with trivial representation). Choice of setting, pinned: scalar-valued, integral weight k, Γ a subgroup of GL₂(ℝ) (in the theorems: the image of a finite-index subgroup of SL₂(ℤ)); the Weil-representation setting of Bruinier–Funke (vector-valued forms of weight k ∈ ½ℤ for ρ_L on Mp₂(ℤ)) specialises to this one for unimodular L and is not built here. Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades' space 'H_k(Γ₀(N), χ)' is the subspace H_k^+ of QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-plus-space.
hypotheses: k ∈ ℤ; theorems exclude k = 1 where BF do.
C² as in BF; real analyticity (BF: 'automatically real analytic') is not part of the definition and not needed by any result here.
proofSteps: Structure extending SlashInvariantForm Γ k with fields contDiff' (ContDiffOn ℝ 2 (f ∘ ofComplex) on the upper half-plane set), harmonic' (Δ_k f = 0 on ℍ), expGrowth' (IsExpGrowthAtCusps Γ k f).
ℂ-module structure: Δ_k and slash are ℂ-linear (det = 1), growth is closed under sums.
M^!_k(Γ) → H_k(Γ): holomorphic functions are annihilated by Δ_k (hyperbolicLaplacian_of_mdifferentiable) and are C^∞.
Restriction to a subgroup Γ′ ≤ Γ: cusps of Γ′ are cusps of Γ for arithmetic groups (finite index).
acceptance: E₂* = E₂ − 3/(πv) ∈ H_2(SL₂(ℤ)) (QM.3/nonholomorphic-eisenstein-series-e2-star), while E₂ is not: E₂|_2S ≠ E₂.
For odd k and −I ∈ Γ, H_k(Γ) = 0.

sources.match: The definition, specialised to the trivial representation (scalar-valued) and integral weight.
The standing hypotheses k ≠ 1, finite index.
Identifies BOR's H_k with BF's H_k^+.

nodes.title: Fourier coefficients of a harmonic Maass form solve the radial ODE
nodes.statement: Let Γ be arithmetic, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, f ∈ H_k(Γ), h = Γ.strictWidthInfty and a(n; v) := h^{−1}∫_0^h f(u + iv)e(−nu/h)du. Then f(u + iv) = Σ_{n∈ℤ} a(n; v)e(nu/h) (absolutely convergent), and there are unique α_n, β_n ∈ ℂ with: a(0; v) = α₀ + β₀v^{1−k}; for n < 0, a(n; v) = α_n e^{−2πnv/h} + β_n Γ(1−k, 4π|n|v/h)e^{−2πnv/h}; for n > 0, a(n; v) = α_n e^{−2πnv/h} + β_n e^{−W}∫_1^W s^{−k}e^{2s}ds with W = 2πnv/h.
hypotheses: k ≠ 1 (for k = 1 the constant term involves log v).
f ∈ H_k(Γ) only (no plus-space condition).
proofSteps: Periodicity f(τ + h) = f(τ) (T^h ∈ Γ); a(n; v) is C² in v (differentiation under the integral, f ∈ C²).

Integrating Δ_k f(u + iv)e(−nu/h) over u ∈ [0, h] and integrating by parts in u (periodicity) gives Δ_k(a(n; v)e(nu/h)) = 0, i.e. v²a″ + kva′ + (kκv − κ²v²)a = 0 with κ = 2πn/h (a = e^{−κv} is a solution); in W = κv this is the ODE b″ − b + (k/W)(b′ + b) = 0 of BF p. 9.
n = 0: v²a″ + kva′ = 0 has solutions 1, v^{1−k} (k ≠ 1).

n ≠ 0: the solution space is 2-dimensional; e^{−W} and the second solutions of QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying (n < 0) and QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-growing (n > 0) are independent solutions.
Fourier series: f(· + iv) is C² and h-periodic, so its Fourier coefficients are O(n^{−2}) and the series converges absolutely (Mathlib's hasSum_fourier_series_of_summable).
acceptance: For f ∈ M^!_k(Γ): β_n = 0 for all n and α_n are the Laurent coefficients of QM.3/weakly-holomorphic-laurent-expansion.
For E₂* (h = 1, k = 2): α₀ = 1, β₀ = −3/π, α_n = −24σ(n) for n > 0, all other coefficients 0.

nodes.title: Growth kills all but finitely many polar coefficients
nodes.statement: In the situation of QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode, exponential growth of f at ∞ implies: α_n = 0 for all but finitely many n < 0, and β_n = 0 for all but finitely many n > 0.
hypotheses: f ∈ H_k(Γ), Γ arithmetic, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1.
proofSteps: |a(n; v)| ≤ sup_u |f(u + iv)| ≤ A e^{Cv} for v ≥ v₀.
For n < 0: the β-term Γ(1−k, 4π|n|v/h)e^{2π|n|v/h} = O(v^{−k}e^{−2π|n|v/h}) is bounded, so α_n e^{2π|n|v/h} = O(e^{Cv}) forces α_n = 0 when 2π|n|/h > C.
For n > 0: the β-term grows like ½W^{−k}e^{W} with W = 2πnv/h, while e^{−W} decays, so β_n = 0 when 2πn/h > C.

nodes.title: ξ_k as a conjugate-linear map H_k(Γ) → M^!_{2−k}(Γ)
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ GL₂(ℝ) be arithmetic with Γ.HasDetOne and k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1. For f ∈ H_k(Γ), ξ_k f (QM.3/xi-operator) is a weakly holomorphic modular form of weight 2 − k for Γ, and f ↦ ξ_k f is a conjugate-linear map ξ_k : H_k(Γ) → M^!_{2−k}(Γ) (Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.2).
hypotheses: Γ arithmetic and Γ.HasDetOne (e.g. the image of a finite-index subgroup of SL₂(ℤ)); k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1.
Conjugate-linear: a σ-semilinear map for σ = complex conjugation (Mathlib's →ₗ⋆[ℂ]).
proofSteps: Holomorphy: f is C² and Δ_k f = 0, so ξ_k f is holomorphic (QM.3/xi-holomorphic-iff-harmonic).
Invariance: (ξ_k f)|_{2−k}γ = ξ_k(f|_kγ) = ξ_k f for γ ∈ Γ (QM.3/xi-slash-equivariance).

Growth at a cusp c = g∞ (g ∈ SL₂(ℤ)): f|_kg ∈ H_k(g^{−1}Γg); expand it by QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode; ξ_k kills the α-terms and maps the β-terms to β̄₀(1−k), −β̄_n(4π|n|/h)^{1−k}e(|n|τ/h) (n < 0) and β̄_n(2πn/h)^{1−k}e(−nτ/h) (n > 0) (QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying/-growing); by QM.3/harmonic-coefficients-eventually-zero only finitely many negative powers occur, so (ξ_k f)|_{2−k}g has exponential growth at ∞; any other g′ with g′∞ = c differs by an upper-triangular matrix.
Conjugate-linearity from xiOperator_add.
acceptance: ξ_2(E₂*) = 3/π, the constant function, an element of M_0(SL₂(ℤ)) ⊆ M^!_0(SL₂(ℤ)).
ξ_k vanishes on the image of M^!_k(Γ).

nodes.title: The subspace H_k^+(Γ) = ξ_k^{−1}(S_{2−k}(Γ))
nodes.statement: For Γ arithmetic with Γ.HasDetOne and k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1: H_k^+(Γ) := {f ∈ H_k(Γ) : ξ_k f is a cusp form}, the preimage of S_{2−k}(Γ) (Mathlib's CuspForm Γ (2 − k)) under ξ_k. It is a ℂ-subspace (ξ_k is additive and S_{2−k} is stable under conjugate scalars). Equivalently (QM.3/plus-space-principal-part-characterisation) at every cusp f minus a Laurent polynomial in q^{−1} decays exponentially — the definition of Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades' H_k.
hypotheses: As in QM.3/xi-map.
proofSteps: Define as the Submodule {f | ∃ g : CuspForm Γ (2−k), ⇑g = ⇑(ξ_k f)}; closure under c·: ξ(cf) = c̄ξf and c̄g is a cusp form.
M^!_k(Γ) ⊆ H_k^+(Γ) since ξ vanishes there.
k ≥ 2: S_{2−k}(Γ) = 0 (weight ≤ 0 cusp forms vanish: negative weight by ModularForm.subsingleton_of_neg_weight in Tau Ceti, weight 0 by constancy), so H_k^+(Γ) = M^!_k(Γ).

nodes.title: Fourier expansion of f ∈ H_k^+(Γ)
nodes.statement: Let Γ be arithmetic with Γ.HasDetOne, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, h = Γ.strictWidthInfty and f ∈ H_k^+(Γ). There are N ∈ ℕ and a⁺, a⁻ : ℤ → ℂ with a⁺(n) = 0 for n < −N, a⁻(n) = 0 for n ≥ 0, such that for all τ ∈ ℍ, f(τ) = Σ_{n∈ℤ} a⁺(n)e(nτ/h) + Σ_{n<0} a⁻(n)Γ(1−k, 4π|n|v/h)e(nτ/h), both series converging absolutely and locally uniformly. The coefficients are unique; a⁺(n) = lim_{v→∞} a(n; v)e^{2πnv/h}. (Bruinier–Funke (3.2) restricted to H^+; Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (1.2) with h = 1 and weight 2 − k.)
hypotheses: k ≠ 1; f ∈ H_k^+ (for f ∈ H_k \ H_k^+ the constant term v^{1−k} and the growing terms ψ_n also occur, see QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode).
proofSteps: Expand by QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode with coefficients α_n, β_n.

ξ_k f = Σ_n (ξ of the β-terms) is a cusp form; its constant term is β̄₀(1−k) and its negative-index terms are β̄_n(2πn/h)^{1−k} (n > 0); uniqueness of Fourier coefficients of ξ_k f gives β₀ = 0 (k ≠ 1) and β_n = 0 for n > 0.
Set a⁺ = α, a⁻ = β; a⁺(n) = 0 for n ≪ 0 by QM.3/harmonic-coefficients-eventually-zero.

Convergence: Σ_{n<0}|a⁻(n)Γ(1−k, 4π|n|v/h)e(nτ/h)| converges since |a⁻(n)| = O(|n|^{k/2}) (QM.3/nonholomorphic-coefficient-bound) and the basis functions are O(v^{−k}e^{−2π|n|v/h}); the a⁺-series is then the difference of two convergent Fourier series.
The limit formula for a⁺(n): Γ(1−k, x) → 0 as x → ∞ and v^{1−k}-term absent.
acceptance: For f ∈ M^!_k(Γ) this is the Laurent expansion with a⁻ = 0.

nodes.title: Holomorphic and non-holomorphic parts f⁺, f⁻ (mock modular forms)
nodes.statement: For f ∈ H_k^+(Γ) (Γ arithmetic, Γ.HasDetOne, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, h = Γ.strictWidthInfty), with a⁺, a⁻ as in QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion: the holomorphic part f⁺(τ) := Σ_n a⁺(n)e(nτ/h) and the non-holomorphic part f⁻ := f − f⁺ = Σ_{n<0} a⁻(n)Γ(1−k, 4π|n|v/h)e(nτ/h). Coefficient functionals: a⁺(n) = lim_{v→∞} (h^{−1}∫_0^h f(u+iv)e(−nu/h)du)·e^{2πnv/h} (defined for every function) and a⁻(n) = the coefficient of Γ(1−k, 4π|n|v/h)e(nτ/h). f⁺ is a mock modular form in Zagier's sense: its shadow is ξ_k f, a cusp form of weight 2 − k.
hypotheses: Defined at the cusp ∞ with the width of Γ; at another cusp σ∞ apply the definition to f|_kσ ∈ H_k^+(σ^{−1}Γσ).
Normalisation pinned: f⁺ carries all holomorphic terms including the constant term a⁺(0); f⁻ has no constant term.
proofSteps: Define holoCoeff f n by the limit formula (a real definition, valid for any function); holomorphicPart f τ := Σ' n, holoCoeff f n · e(nτ/h).
By QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion the limit exists and equals a⁺(n), and f = f⁺ + f⁻.
f⁺ is holomorphic on ℍ (locally uniform limit of holomorphic partial sums with finitely many negative terms).
ξ_k f = ξ_k f⁻ since ξ_k f⁺ = 0; f⁻ = O(v^{−k}e^{−2πv/h}) as v → ∞.
acceptance: For f ∈ M^!_k(Γ): f⁺ = f and f⁻ = 0.
For Q(−m, k, N): f⁺ = q^{−m} + O(1) at ∞.

sources.match: f⁺ and f⁻ as in (3.2a), (3.2b).
Same definitions in weight 2 − k.

nodes.title: The principal part P(f)
nodes.statement: For f ∈ H_k^+(Γ) as in QM.3/holomorphic-part, P(f) := Σ_{n≤0} a⁺(n)T^n ∈ ℂ[T, T^{−1}] (a Laurent polynomial by QM.3/harmonic-coefficients-eventually-zero), read as the Fourier polynomial P(f)(τ) = Σ_{n≤0} a⁺(n)e(nτ/h) (Bruinier–Funke (3.6)). It includes the constant term a⁺(0).
hypotheses: At the cusp ∞ with the width h of Γ; at σ∞ use f|_kσ.
proofSteps: Finite support: a⁺(n) = 0 for n < −N.
Build the Laurent polynomial Σ_{−N≤n≤0} a⁺(n)T^n (Mathlib's LaurentPolynomial).
Linearity from the linearity of the coefficient functionals.
acceptance: f − P(f)(q_h) = O(e^{−εv}) for f ∈ H_k^+ (BF p. 11).

nodes.title: H_k^+ via exponential decay after removing a principal part
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, f ∈ H_k(Γ). Then f ∈ H_k^+(Γ) if and only if for every σ ∈ SL₂(ℤ) there are a Laurent polynomial P_σ ∈ ℂ[T^{−1}] and ε > 0 with (f|_kσ)(τ) − P_σ(e(τ/h_σ)) = O(e^{−εv}) as v → ∞, h_σ the width of σ^{−1}Γσ at ∞. This is the definition of Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades' space H_k(Γ₀(N), χ) (their condition (iii)), so their H_k is BF's H_k^+.
hypotheses: Finite-index Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ), so every cusp is σ∞ with σ ∈ SL₂(ℤ).
proofSteps: ⇒: f|_kσ ∈ H_k^+(σ^{−1}Γσ) since ξ_k(f|_kσ) = (ξ_kf)|_{2−k}σ is a cusp form for σ^{−1}Γσ; its expansion (QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion) minus its principal part is Σ_{n>0}a⁺(n)q_h^n + Σ_{n<0}a⁻(n)Γ(1−k, 4π|n|v/h)q_h^n = O(e^{−εv}).

⇐: in the expansion of QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode for f|_kσ, the terms β₀v^{1−k} (k ≠ 1) and β_nψ_n (n > 0) do not decay and are not Laurent polynomials in q, so decay forces β₀ = 0 and β_n = 0 for n > 0; then ξ_k(f|_kσ) has only positive powers of q, i.e. ξ_k f vanishes at every cusp.
acceptance: E₂* fails the condition at ∞: E₂* − 1 = −3/(πv) + O(e^{−2πv}) is not O(e^{−εv}).

sources.match: The right-hand side of the equivalence.
The equivalence, asserted by BF.

nodes.title: Fourier expansion of ξ_k f
nodes.statement: For f ∈ H_k^+(Γ) with expansion as in QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion: ξ_k f(τ) = −Σ_{n<0} \overline{a⁻(n)}(4π|n|/h)^{1−k} e(|n|τ/h). Equivalently, with b(m) the coefficients of the cusp form ξ_k f: b(m) = −\overline{a⁻(−m)}(4πm/h)^{1−k} for m ≥ 1 (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (1.3), with h = 1 and weight 2 − k). This corrects the constant in Bruinier–Funke Lemma 3.1 (factor 1, not 2; sourceIssue E401).
proofSteps: Apply ξ_k termwise (locally uniform convergence of the series and of its ∂̄-derivatives on compacta) and use QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying.
Conjugate-linearity of ξ_k turns a⁻(n) into \overline{a⁻(n)}.
acceptance: For Q(−m, k, N): a⁻(−m) = −1/(k−2)! gives the leading coefficient (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)! of ξ_{2−k}Q(−m, k, N), matching BOR §6.2.

sources.match: Exactly the statement (weight 2 − k, width 1).

nodes.title: Growth of harmonic Maass forms towards the real axis
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index and f ∈ H_k(Γ). Then there are A, C > 0 with |f(u + iv)| ≤ A e^{C/v} for all u ∈ ℝ and 0 < v ≤ 1 (Bruinier–Funke Lemma 3.3). (The same bound for f⁺, f⁻ is part of QM.3/holomorphic-coefficient-bound.)
hypotheses: Γ of finite index in SL₂(ℤ) (finitely many cosets).
proofSteps: For τ = u + iv with v ≤ 1 choose γ = (a b; c d) ∈ SL₂(ℤ) with w := γτ in the standard fundamental domain (ModularGroup.exists_smul_mem_fd), so Im w ≥ √3/2.
Then f(τ) = j(γ, τ)^{−k}·(f|_kγ^{−1})(w) with j(γ, τ) = cτ + d, and f|_kγ^{−1} = f|_kγ₀ for γ₀ in a finite set R of representatives of Γ\SL₂(ℤ) (f is Γ-invariant).
Im w = v/|cτ + d|² ≤ 1/v if c ≠ 0 and Im w = v ≤ 1 if c = 0; hence √3/2 ≤ Im w ≤ 1/v and |j(γ, τ)|^{−k} = (Im w/v)^{k/2} ≤ A₁v^{−|k|}.
Each f|_kγ₀ (γ₀ ∈ R) is continuous with exponential growth at ∞, so |(f|_kγ₀)(w)| ≤ A₂e^{C Im w} on the fundamental domain; together |f(τ)| ≤ A₁A₂v^{−|k|}e^{C/v} ≤ A e^{(C+1)/v}.
The constant C is uniform because R is finite.
acceptance: For f = 1/Δ: |1/Δ(iv)| = v^{12}|1/Δ(i/v)| grows like v^{12}e^{2π/v} as v → 0.

sources.match: Exactly the statement.

nodes.title: Polynomial bound for the non-holomorphic coefficients a⁻(n)
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, f ∈ H_k^+(Γ), and let β_n (n < 0) be the coefficients of the decaying basis functions in QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode (width h). If b(m) (m ≥ 1) are the Fourier coefficients of the cusp form ξ_k f, then b(m) = −\overline{β_{−m}}(4πm/h)^{1−k}, and consequently β_{−m} = O(m^{k/2}) as m → ∞ (Bruinier–Funke Lemma 3.4, second part).
hypotheses: f ∈ H_k^+; the identity is proved mode by mode, before the full expansion is known to converge.
proofSteps: The m-th Fourier coefficient (in u) of ξ_k f at height v is ξ_k applied to the (−m)-th Fourier mode of f: differentiation under the integral sign for the C¹ periodic function f(· + iv) and ξ_k f = 2iv^k·conj(∂̄f).

By QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode and QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying (α-terms are holomorphic, killed by ξ) this is −\overline{β_{−m}}(4πm/h)^{1−k}e(mτ/h); compare with b(m)e(mτ/h).
Hecke's bound b(m) = O(m^{(2−k)/2}) for the cusp form ξ_k f (Mathlib CuspFormClass.qExpansion_isBigO, width h) gives |β_{−m}| = O(m^{(2−k)/2 − (1−k)}) = O(m^{k/2}).
acceptance: For f ∈ M^!_k(Γ) all β_n vanish, matching ξ_k f = 0.
For Q(−m, k, N) in weight 2 − k: β_{−m} = −1/(k−2)! gives b(m) = (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!, the leading coefficient of ξ_{2−k}Q(−m, k, N) = (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!·P(m, k, N) (BOR §6.2).

sources.match: Exactly the bound.
The proof, via (3.7) (whose constant carries the factor-2 slip of Lemma 3.1, E401; the bound is unaffected).

nodes.title: Subexponential bound for the holomorphic coefficients a⁺(n)
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, f ∈ H_k^+(Γ). Then f⁺ and f⁻ satisfy the bound of QM.3/harmonic-growth-near-real-axis, and there is C > 0 with a⁺(n) = O(e^{C√n}) as n → +∞ (Bruinier–Funke Lemma 3.4, first part).
proofSteps: For integer k ≠ 1 the integral definition and recurrence of Γ give the uniform bound |Γ(1−k, x)e^{x/2}| ≤ C(1 + x^{−max(k,0)})e^{−x/4} for x > 0: bound the integral separately on 0 < x ≤ 1 and x ≥ 1, absorbing the large-x polynomial into e^{x/4}. The asymptotic C x^{−k}e^{−x/2} alone is not a bound for small x when k ≤ 0. Multiply by |a⁻(−m)| = O(m^{k/2}) (QM.3/nonholomorphic-coefficient-bound) and sum at x = 4πmv/h. Exponentially weighted power sums give |f⁻(τ)| ≤ A v^{−N} ≤ A′e^{1/v} for 0 < v ≤ 1 and some integer N; then f⁺ = f − f⁻ satisfies |f⁺| ≤ A e^{C/v} (QM.3/harmonic-growth-near-real-axis).
a⁺(n) = h^{−1}∫_0^h f⁺(u + iv)e(−n(u + iv)/h)du for every v > 0, so |a⁺(n)| ≤ A e^{C/v}e^{2πnv/h}; take v = 1/√n.
acceptance: For Q(−1, 12, 1): a⁺(n) grows like const·n^{−11/2}·I_{11}(4π√n), i.e. like e^{4π√n}n^{−23/4}, consistent with O(e^{C√n}).

sources.match: The a⁺ bound (the a⁻ bound on H^+ is superseded by QM.3/nonholomorphic-coefficient-bound).
The bound for f⁺ and f⁻ (first proof step).

nodes.title: Stokes' theorem on the truncated fundamental domain
nodes.statement: Let F_T := {τ ∈ ℍ : |τ| ≥ 1, |Re τ| ≤ 1/2, Im τ ≤ T} (T > 1) and let G be a C¹ function on a neighbourhood of F_T. Then ∫_{F_T} ∂_τ̄ G(τ) du dv = (1/(2i))∮_{∂F_T} G(τ) dτ, with ∂F_T positively oriented (the boundary path is Tau Ceti's TauCeti.ModularForm.fdBoundary T). In the form used by Bruinier–Funke: for the 1-form ω = G dτ, dω = ∂_τ̄G dτ̄ ∧ dτ = 2i ∂_τ̄G du ∧ dv.
hypotheses: G of class C¹ on an open set containing F_T; T > 1.
proofSteps: F_T = {(u, v) : |u| ≤ ½, φ(u) ≤ v ≤ T} with φ(u) = √(1 − u²) is vertically simple.
∫∫ ∂_v G dv du = ∫_{−1/2}^{1/2}[G(u, T) − G(u, φ(u))]du by the fundamental theorem of calculus in v and Fubini (MeasureTheory.integral_prod).
∫∫ ∂_u G dv du: differentiate u ↦ ∫_{φ(u)}^T G(u, v)dv (Leibniz rule with variable lower limit) and integrate in u: ∫∫∂_uG = [∫_{φ(u)}^T G dv]_{u=−1/2}^{1/2} + ∫ G(u, φ(u))φ′(u)du.
Combine ∂̄ = ½(∂_u + i∂_v) and compare with the four boundary pieces of fdBoundary T (right side, top, left side, arc).
acceptance: For G = τ̄ (∂̄G = 1): (1/(2i))∮_{∂F_T} τ̄ dτ equals the Euclidean area T − π/6 − √3/4 of F_T.
For holomorphic G both sides vanish (Cauchy's theorem on F_T).

sources.match: The Stokes step used in Prop. 3.5, on exactly this domain.

nodes.title: The Bruinier–Funke pairing {g, f}
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, κ := 2 − k. For g ∈ M_κ(Γ) (Mathlib's ModularForm Γ κ) and f ∈ H_k^+(Γ): {g, f} := (g, ξ_k f)_κ, the Petersson product of the modular form g with the cusp form ξ_k f, (g, h)_κ := Σ_{q ∈ SL₂(ℤ)/Γ̃} ∫_{F} (g|_κq^{−1})(τ)·\overline{(h|_κq^{−1})(τ)}·v^κ dμ(τ), where Γ̃ = Γ·{±I}, F = ModularGroup.fd and dμ = du dv/v² is Mathlib's measure on ℍ (an unnormalised integral over Γ̃\ℍ). In Tau Ceti's notation (g, h)_κ = Σ_q UpperHalfPlane.peterssonInner κ F (h|q^{−1}) (g|q^{−1}), which for a cusp form g is CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets h g. The pairing is ℂ-bilinear (ξ_k is conjugate-linear and the Petersson product conjugate-linear in h).
hypotheses: Γ of finite index in SL₂(ℤ) (viewed in GL₂(ℝ)); k ≠ 1.
Convention pinned: linear in g, and linear in f; the Petersson product is not normalised by the index.
proofSteps: Each summand is integrable: g|q^{−1} is a modular form and (ξ_kf)|q^{−1} a cusp form for q^{−1}Γq, bounded by Tau Ceti's integrableOn_petersson_sl_smul_fd_left/right.
Independence of the coset representatives: g|(qδ)^{−1} = g|q^{−1} for δ ∈ Γ̃ up to the sign (−1)^κ, which cancels between g and \overline{h} since both have weight κ.
Bilinearity from the sesquilinearity of the integral and the conjugate-linearity of ξ_k.
acceptance: {g, f} = 0 for f ∈ M^!_k(Γ).
For level one, g ∈ S_κ and Q(−m, k′, 1) with k′ = κ: {g, Q(−m)} = b_g(m), the m-th coefficient of g (QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing-formula).

sources.match: Exactly the definition (scalar case).
The Petersson product, linear in the first variable.

nodes.title: {g, f} in terms of principal parts
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, κ = 2 − k, g ∈ M_κ(Γ), f ∈ H_k^+(Γ). For each cusp c of Γ choose σ_c ∈ SL₂(ℤ) with σ_c∞ = c and let h_c be the width, a⁺_c(n) the holomorphic coefficients of f|_kσ_c and b_c(n) the coefficients of g|_κσ_c (in e(nτ/h_c)). Write w_c for the geometric cusp width (possibly h_c/2). Then {g, f} = Σ_{c ∈ Γ\ℙ¹(ℚ)} w_c Σ_{n≤0} a⁺_c(n) b_c(−n). In particular the pairing depends only on the principal parts of f at the cusps. For Γ = SL₂(ℤ): {g, f} = Σ_{n≤0} a⁺(n)b(−n) (Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.5).
hypotheses: Finite-index Γ; the choice of σ_c does not matter (another choice changes both expansions by the same translation).
Fourier coefficients use the strict period h_c. Cusp-sum weights are w_c := widthInfty(σ_c^{−1}Γσ_c), the orbit length for Γ·{±I}; w_c = h_c at regular cusps and w_c = h_c/2 at irregular cusps.
proofSteps: Pointwise: g·\overline{ξ_kf}·v^κ = g·L_kf (since \overline{ξ_kf} = v^{k−2}L_kf), and d(g f dτ) = ∂̄(gf)dτ̄∧dτ = −g L_k f dμ (g holomorphic).
For each coset q apply QM.3/truncated-fundamental-domain-stokes to G_q = (g|q^{−1})(f|q^{−1}) on F_T; the integral over F converges and is the limit T → ∞.
Sum over q ∈ SL₂(ℤ)/Γ̃: the two vertical sides cancel after reindexing q ↦ T^{−1}q (the form G_q dτ has weight 2), the arc cancels after q ↦ S^{−1}q.

Top edges: the cosets in one orbit of q ↦ Tq correspond to a cusp c and there are w_c of them (Γ̃ counts ±); the sum of their top integrals is (w_c/h_c)∫_0^{h_c}(g|σ_c)(f|σ_c)(u + iT)du = w_c·(constant term) = w_c Σ_{n≤0}a⁺_c(n)b_c(−n) + (terms Γ(1−k, 4π|n|T/h_c)·b_c(−n) → 0).
Let T → ∞.
acceptance: For level one and f = Q(−m, κ, 1), g = E_κ (Eisenstein series, orthogonal to cusp forms): 0 = a⁺(0) + b_{E_κ}(m); for m = 1, κ = 12 this gives a⁺(0) = −65520/691, which BOR Prop. 6.2 confirms numerically (BOR's introduction prints −0.04629; sourceIssue E405).
{g, f} = 0 for f ∈ M^!_k(Γ) gives Σ_c w_c Σ_{n≤0} a_c(n)b_c(−n) = 0, the residue theorem for f g dτ on X(Γ).

sources.match: The level-one statement.
The finite-index generalisation; the cusp-sum form is the one used by BOR Theorem 4.1.
Same Stokes argument with widths w_κ at the cusps.

nodes.title: Finite-index subgroups contain a normal subgroup acting freely
nodes.statement: Every finite-index subgroup Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) contains a subgroup Γ″ of finite index in SL₂(ℤ), normal in SL₂(ℤ), that acts freely on ℍ; one may take Γ″ = Γ(3) ∩ core(Γ), where core(Γ) = ⋂_{g} gΓg^{−1} is the normal core and Γ(3) the principal congruence subgroup of level 3.
hypotheses: Γ of finite index in SL₂(ℤ).
proofSteps: core(Γ) is normal of finite index (Subgroup.normalCore_normal, Subgroup.finiteIndex_normalCore); Γ(3) is normal (CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma_normal) of finite index; their intersection is normal of finite index.

Stabilizers of points of ℍ in SL₂(ℤ) are finite (Tau Ceti's TauCeti.ModularGroup.finite_stabilizer) and consist of ±I and elliptic elements, whose traces lie in {0, ±1}; an element of Γ(3) has trace ≡ 2 mod 3, so traces 0 and 1 are excluded; trace −1 would mean γ² + γ + I = 0 with γ = I + 3A, i.e. 3(I + 3A + 3A²) = 0, impossible mod 3; and −I ∉ Γ(3).
Hence the stabilizer in Γ″ of every point is trivial: Γ″ acts freely.
acceptance: For Γ = SL₂(ℤ): Γ″ = Γ(3), of index 24, acting freely on ℍ.

sources.match: The existence of such Γ″ is used without proof; this lemma supplies it.

nodes.title: Local ξ-preimages near a cusp
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, g ∈ M^!_{2−k}(Γ), σ ∈ SL₂(ℤ), h the width of σ^{−1}Γσ at ∞ and (g|_{2−k}σ)(τ) = Σ_{m≥−N} b(m)e(mτ/h). Then F_σ(τ) := Σ_{m≥1} −\overline{b(m)}(4πm/h)^{k−1}Γ(1−k, 4πmv/h)e(−mτ/h) + \overline{b(0)}(1−k)^{−1}v^{1−k} + Σ_{m=1}^{N}\overline{b(−m)}(2πm/h)^{k−1}ψ_m(τ), with ψ_m as in QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-growing (weight k, width h), converges absolutely and locally uniformly on ℍ with all derivatives, is h-periodic and C^∞, satisfies Δ_k F_σ = 0, and ξ_k F_σ = g|_{2−k}σ on ℍ.
hypotheses: k ≠ 1 (the constant term needs (1 − k)^{−1}).
No invariance beyond the translations T^h is claimed: F_σ is only used near the cusp.
proofSteps: Termwise, by QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying (ξ of the Γ-terms gives b(m)e(mτ/h) after conjugation), ξ_k(v^{1−k}) = 1 − k, and QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-growing (ξ of ψ_m gives (2πm/h)^{1−k}e(−mτ/h)).

Convergence: Σ|b(m)|e^{−2πmv/h} < ∞ for every v > 0 (Laurent expansion of g|σ converges absolutely), on each compact subset of ℍ all sufficiently large m have x≥1, where |Γ(1−k, x)e^{x/2}| ≤ Cx^{−k}e^{−x/2}; the derivative series have analogous large-x bounds with polynomial factors, absorbed by comparing the Laurent expansion at half the compact set’s minimum height; finitely many smaller m are smooth.
ξ_k is applied termwise (locally uniform convergence of the derivative series).
acceptance: For g = 3/π (weight 0, level one, k = 2): F = −(3/π)v^{−1}, the non-holomorphic part of E₂*.

sources.match: BF's claim that this (0,1)-form is a smooth section near the cusps is not justified (sourceIssue E406); the explicit local preimage F_σ repairs the argument near each cusp.

nodes.title: ξ_k is surjective for a normal subgroup acting freely
nodes.statement: Let Γ″ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) be of finite index, normal in SL₂(ℤ) and acting freely on ℍ, and k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1. Then ξ_k : H_k(Γ″) → M^!_{2−k}(Γ″) is surjective (Bruinier–Funke Thm. 3.7 for Γ″, repaired at the cusps).
hypotheses: Γ″ acts freely on ℍ, so X = X(Γ″) is a compact Riemann surface with no elliptic points and the weight-k forms form a holomorphic line bundle L_k on X (holomorphic at the cusps); D = sum of the cusps.
proofSteps: Let g ∈ M^!_{2−k}(Γ″). For each cusp c = σ_c∞ take F_c := F_{σ_c}∘σ_c^{−1} slashed back (QM.3/local-xi-preimage-at-cusps) and a smooth cut-off χ_c on X equal to 1 near c and supported in a small punctured disc; f₀ := Σ_c χ_c F_c is a smooth weight-k function on ℍ with ξ_k f₀ = g near every cusp.
The (0,1)-form ω := (i/2)v^{−k}\overline{(g − ξ_k f₀)}dτ̄ is a smooth section of E^{0,1}(X, L_k) with compact support in X minus the cusps.
Dolbeault: H¹(X, L_k ⊗ O_{nD}) ≅ E^{0,1}(X, L_k ⊗ O_{nD})/∂̄E^{0,0}(X, L_k ⊗ O_{nD}) (upstream: Tau Ceti ModularForms 10B, Dolbeault resolution of an invertible sheaf).

Serre duality with the cusp twist K_X ≅ L_2(−D): H¹(X, L_k ⊗ O_{nD}) ≅ H⁰(X, L_{2−k} ⊗ O_{−(n+1)D})^*, which is 0 for n large because a non-zero form of weight 2 − k has a bounded number of zeros (valence bound) (upstream: Tau Ceti ModularForms 10B (iv) for invertible sheaves, 10C automorphy line bundles).
So ω = ∂̄f₁ with f₁ a smooth section of L_k ⊗ O_{nD}, i.e. a smooth weight-k Γ″-invariant function with exponential growth at the cusps and ∂_τ̄f₁ = (i/2)v^{−k}\overline{(g − ξ_kf₀)}.
f := f₀ + f₁ satisfies ξ_k f = 2iv^k\overline{∂̄f} = ξ_kf₀ + (g − ξ_kf₀) = g, which is holomorphic, so Δ_k f = 0 (QM.3/xi-holomorphic-iff-harmonic): f ∈ H_k(Γ″).
acceptance: For Γ″ = Γ(3), k = 2, g = 3/π this produces E₂* up to M^!_2(Γ(3)).

nodes.title: Descent of ξ-preimages along a normal subgroup
nodes.statement: Let Γ″ ⊴ Γ be arithmetic subgroups with finite index [Γ : Γ″], k ∈ ℤ, and g ∈ M^!_{2−k}(Γ). If f″ ∈ H_k(Γ″) satisfies ξ_k f″ = g, then f := [Γ : Γ″]^{−1}Σ_{γ ∈ Γ″\Γ} f″|_kγ lies in H_k(Γ) and ξ_k f = g.
hypotheses: Γ″ normal in Γ, of finite index; Γ.HasDetOne.
proofSteps: Γ″ normal ⇒ f″|_kγ ∈ H_k(Γ″) for γ ∈ Γ (slash-invariance under γ^{−1}Γ″γ = Γ″, Δ_k equivariance, growth at the permuted cusps), and the sum over Γ″\Γ is well defined and Γ-invariant.
ξ_k(f″|_kγ) = (ξ_kf″)|_{2−k}γ = g|_{2−k}γ = g (QM.3/xi-slash-equivariance and Γ-invariance of g), so ξ_k f = g.
acceptance: This is BF's 'cohomology of a finite group acting on a ℂ-vector space vanishes', made explicit as averaging.

nodes.title: Surjectivity of ξ_k (Bruinier–Funke Theorem 3.7)
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index and k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1. Then ξ_k : H_k(Γ) → M^!_{2−k}(Γ) is surjective.
hypotheses: Finite index in SL₂(ℤ); k ≠ 1.
proofSteps: Choose Γ″ ≤ Γ normal in SL₂(ℤ), of finite index, acting freely on ℍ (QM.3/normal-torsion-free-subgroup); Γ″ is normal in Γ.
g ∈ M^!_{2−k}(Γ) ⊆ M^!_{2−k}(Γ″); take f″ ∈ H_k(Γ″) with ξ_kf″ = g (QM.3/xi-surjective-free-normal).
Average over Γ″\Γ (QM.3/xi-surjective-descent).
acceptance: k = 2, Γ = SL₂(ℤ), g = 3/π: a preimage is E₂*.
k ≥ 2 with 2 − k < 0: every weakly holomorphic form of negative weight 2 − k is a ξ-image (e.g. of harmonic forms built from Poincaré series).

nodes.title: The exact sequences 0 → M^!_k → H_k → M^!_{2−k} → 0 and 0 → M^!_k → H_k^+ → S_{2−k} → 0
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, the sequences 0 → M^!_k(Γ) → H_k(Γ) → M^!_{2−k}(Γ) → 0 and 0 → M^!_k(Γ) → H_k^+(Γ) → S_{2−k}(Γ) → 0 (the second map is ξ_k) are exact (Bruinier–Funke Cor. 3.8).
hypotheses: As in QM.3/xi-surjective. The maps are ℂ-linear (inclusion) and conjugate-linear (ξ_k); exactness is as sets/additive groups.
proofSteps: Injectivity of M^!_k → H_k: toHarmonic is injective.
Exactness in the middle: QM.3/xi-kernel-weakly-holomorphic.
Surjectivity of the first sequence: QM.3/xi-surjective.
Second sequence: for h ∈ S_{2−k}(Γ) ⊆ M^!_{2−k}(Γ) any ξ-preimage lies in H_k^+ by definition; kernel as before.
acceptance: k = 2, Γ = SL₂(ℤ): ξ_2 maps H_2 onto M^!_0 with E₂* ↦ 3/π, and H_2^+ = M^!_2 since S_0 = 0.
k ≤ 0 even, level one: dim H_k^+/M^!_k = dim S_{2−k}(SL₂(ℤ)), e.g. 1 for k = −10.

sources.match: Exactly the statement (ξ_k on the arrows).

nodes.title: Non-degeneracy of {·,·} on H_k^+/M^!_k × S_{2−k} (Bruinier–Funke Theorem 3.6)
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1: (a) if g ∈ S_{2−k}(Γ) and {g, f} = 0 for all f ∈ H_k^+(Γ) then g = 0; (b) if f ∈ H_k^+(Γ) and {g, f} = 0 for all g ∈ S_{2−k}(Γ) then f ∈ M^!_k(Γ). Hence {·,·} induces a perfect pairing between H_k^+(Γ)/M^!_k(Γ) and S_{2−k}(Γ) (finite-dimensional).
hypotheses: As before.
proofSteps: (a) By QM.3/xi-surjective choose f ∈ H_k^+ with ξ_kf = g; then 0 = {g, f} = (g, g) forces g = 0 (Tau Ceti CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets_definite).
(b) Take g = ξ_kf ∈ S_{2−k}: (ξ_kf, ξ_kf) = 0 gives ξ_kf = 0, so f ∈ M^!_k (QM.3/xi-kernel-weakly-holomorphic).

sources.match: Exactly the statement and the reduction.

nodes.title: The pairing {g, f}′ over negative indices
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, g ∈ M_{2−k}(Γ) and f ∈ H_k^+(Γ): {g, f}′ := Σ_{c ∈ Γ\ℙ¹(ℚ)} w_c Σ_{n<0} a⁺_c(n)b_c(−n) (notation of QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing-formula); for Γ = SL₂(ℤ), {g, f}′ = Σ_{n<0}a⁺(n)b(−n) (Bruinier–Funke (3.15)). It differs from {g, f} by the constant-term contribution Σ_c w_c a⁺_c(0)b_c(0).
hypotheses: Same data as the pairing formula.
Fourier coefficients use the strict period h_c. Cusp-sum weights are w_c := widthInfty(σ_c^{−1}Γσ_c), the orbit length for Γ·{±I}; w_c = h_c at regular cusps and w_c = h_c/2 at irregular cusps.
proofSteps: Finite sums: a⁺_c(n) = 0 for n ≪ 0.
{g, f} − {g, f}′ = Σ_c w_c a⁺_c(0)b_c(0) by QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing-formula.
If g ∈ S_{2−k} (all b_c(0) = 0) then {g, f}′ = {g, f}.
acceptance: {g, f}′ = {g, f} for cusp forms g; for f = E₂* ∉ H^+ the pairing is not defined.

nodes.title: The subspace M^!!_k(Γ)
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and k ∈ ℤ: M^!!_k(Γ) := {f ∈ M^!_k(Γ) : Σ_c w_c a_c(0)b_c(0) = 0 for every g ∈ M_{2−k}(Γ)}, the weakly holomorphic forms whose constant terms are orthogonal to the constant terms of all holomorphic modular forms of weight 2 − k (Bruinier–Funke p. 15, scalar case). For f ∈ M^!!_k or g ∈ S_{2−k}: {g, f} = {g, f}′.
hypotheses: Finite-index Γ.
Fourier coefficients use the strict period h_c. Cusp-sum weights are w_c := widthInfty(σ_c^{−1}Γσ_c), the orbit length for Γ·{±I}; w_c = h_c at regular cusps and w_c = h_c/2 at irregular cusps.
proofSteps: A submodule: the condition is linear in f.

If M_{2−k}(Γ) realises every tuple of constant terms at the cusps (Eisenstein series of weight 2 − k ≥ 3), M^!!_k(Γ) is the space of f with vanishing constant terms at all cusps (BF p. 15); at level one this holds for every even k < 0, and M^!!_0 = M^!_0 because M_2(SL₂(ℤ)) = 0.

nodes.title: Spaces of principal parts and the residue pairing
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index with cusp classes c (representatives σ_c, widths h_c): Sing_k(Γ) := the subspace of ⊕_c ℂ[q_c^{−1}] consisting of Laurent polynomials in q_c = e(τ/h_c) with non-positive exponents whose Fourier polynomials are invariant under the weight-k slash action of each cusp stabilizer (including constant terms), PowSer(Γ) := ⊕_c ℂ[[q_c]], and the residue pairing of weight-(2−k) expansions with weight-k principal parts ⟨F, P⟩ := Σ_c w_c Σ_{n≥0} F_c(n)P_c(−n) = Σ_c w_c Res_{q_c=0}(F_cP_c q_c^{−1}dq_c) (Borcherds, GKZ §3, scalar case). The maps λ : M^!_k(Γ) → Sing_k(Γ) (principal parts with constant terms at all cusps) and λ : M_{2−k}(Γ) → PowSer(Γ) (expansions at all cusps).
hypotheses: Scalar integral weight, with local stabilizer compatibility retained. If −I ∈ Γ and k is odd, Sing_k(Γ) = 0. At an irregular cusp with h_c = 2w_c, only exponents n ≡ k (mod 2) are allowed. The geometric residue coefficient is w_c/(2πi), since products of the two weights descend with period w_c.
Fourier coefficients use the strict period h_c. Cusp-sum weights are w_c := widthInfty(σ_c^{−1}Γσ_c), the orbit length for Γ·{±I}; w_c = h_c at regular cusps and w_c = h_c/2 at irregular cusps.
proofSteps: Define the finite cusp-indexed families and their subspace of non-positive Laurent polynomials. Impose IsCompatiblePrincipalPart Γ k P: for every cusp c, its Fourier polynomial is fixed by the weight-k slash action of the stabilizer of ∞ in σ_c^{−1}Γσ_c. Closure is linear. Use h_c for its Fourier exponents and w_c for the residue/orbit weight.
The pairing is well defined (finite sums) and independent of the representatives σ_c up to the common translation.

nodes.title: Borcherds' obstruction theorem (Serre duality for principal parts)
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index and k ∈ ℤ. A principal part P ∈ Sing_k(Γ) is the principal part (with constant terms) of some f ∈ M^!_k(Γ) if and only if ⟨λ(g), P⟩ = 0 for every g ∈ M_{2−k}(Γ). Equivalently λ(M^!_k(Γ)) = λ(M_{2−k}(Γ))^⊥ and the obstruction space Sing_k(Γ)/λ(M^!_k(Γ)) is dual to M_{2−k}(Γ) (Borcherds, GKZ Theorem 3.1, scalar case with Borcherds' k replaced by 2 − k).
hypotheses: Scalar case; Γ of finite index in SL₂(ℤ).
Fourier coefficients use the strict period h_c. Cusp-sum weights are w_c := widthInfty(σ_c^{−1}Γσ_c), the orbit length for Γ·{±I}; w_c = h_c at regular cusps and w_c = h_c/2 at irregular cusps.
P is cusp-stabilizer-compatible in weight k as defined in QM.3/principal-part-residue-pairing; arbitrary raw Laurent families are not allowed.
proofSteps: Necessity: QM.3/principal-part-residue-pairing (residue theorem for the meromorphic differential f g dτ on X(Γ)).

Sufficiency for Γ″ acting freely: identify H⁰(L_{2−k}) with M_{2−k}, the obstruction space with H¹(X, L_k ⊗ L_cusp^∗) (Mittag-Leffler for sections with prescribed singularities at the cusps), and apply Serre duality H¹(L_k ⊗ L_cusp^∗)^∗ ≅ H⁰(Ω ⊗ L_cusp ⊗ L_{−k}) = H⁰(L_{2−k}) (Ω ≅ L_2 ⊗ L_cusp^∗), the pairing being the sum of residues (upstream: Tau Ceti ModularForms 10B (iv), 10C).
General Γ: pass to Γ″ ⊴ Γ (QM.3/normal-torsion-free-subgroup) and take Γ/Γ″-invariants of a perfect Γ/Γ″-equivariant duality (complete reducibility of finite-group representations over ℂ).
acceptance: Level one, k = 0: T^{−1} + c is realised (by j + c − 744) for every c since M_2(SL₂(ℤ)) = 0.

Level one, k = −10: T^{−1} + c is realised iff ⟨λ(E₁₂), T^{−1} + c⟩ = 65520/691 + c = 0 and ⟨λ(Δ), ·⟩ = 1 = 0 — never; so no weakly holomorphic form of weight −10 has principal part q^{−1} + c (the obstruction is Δ).

sources.match: Theorem 3.1 includes the stabilizer-character compatibility omitted by the original scalar extraction; the theorem conclusion follows in the next sentence. Weight-k principal-part compatibility is retained here.
The Serre-duality step.

nodes.title: Non-degeneracy of {·,·}′ (Bruinier–Funke Corollary 3.9)
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, k ≠ 2, the pairing {·,·}′ induces non-degenerate pairings between H_k^+(Γ)/M^!!_k(Γ) and M_{2−k}(Γ), and between H_k^+(Γ)/M^!_k(Γ) and S_{2−k}(Γ).
hypotheses: As before.
Fourier coefficients use the strict period h_c. Cusp-sum weights are w_c := widthInfty(σ_c^{−1}Γσ_c), the orbit length for Γ·{±I}; w_c = h_c at regular cusps and w_c = h_c/2 at irregular cusps.

Exclude k=2: for scalar level one, g=1 ∈ M_0 is nonzero but has b(n)=0 for all n>0, so {1,f}′=0 for every f. The source Corollary 3.9 is false in this case (E409). The ordinary cusp-form pairing remains non-degenerate at k=2.
proofSteps: Second pairing: {g, f}′ = {g, f} for g ∈ S_{2−k}, so this is QM.3/bruinier-funke-duality.
{g, f}′ = 0 for f ∈ M^!!_k: {g, f} = 0 (f ∈ M^!) and the constant-term correction vanishes by definition of M^!!.

Left kernel: let g ∈ M_{2−k} with {g, f}′ = 0 for all f ∈ H_k^+. If g ∈ S_{2−k}, g = 0 by QM.3/bruinier-funke-duality. Otherwise some b_c(0) ≠ 0; by QM.3/borcherds-obstruction-theorem the realisable principal parts are λ(M_{2−k})^⊥, and if the functional P ↦ Σ_c w_c P_c(0)b_c(0) vanished on λ(M_{2−k})^⊥ it would lie in the finite-dimensional λ(M_{2−k}), giving g′ ∈ M_{2−k} with all non-constant coefficients 0, hence constant, hence 0 for 2 − k ≠ 0 — contradiction; so some f ∈ M^!_k has {g, f}′ = −Σ w_c a_c(0)b_c(0) ≠ 0.
Right kernel: f ∈ H_k^+ with {g, f}′ = 0 ∀ g ∈ M_{2−k}: then f ∈ M^!_k (take g cusp forms and QM.3/bruinier-funke-duality), and then the constant-term condition says f ∈ M^!!_k.
acceptance: Level one, k = −10: E₁₂ pairs non-trivially with Q(−1, 12, 1) under {·,·}′ (value 65520/691).

sources.match: The source claim requires excluding scalar k=2; E409 records a counterexample. The proof below applies when 2−k≠0.

nodes.title: Harmonic Maass forms with prescribed principal parts (Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.11)
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1. For every cusp-stabilizer-compatible family (Q_c)_c in Sing_k(Γ) of Laurent polynomials in q_c^{−1} with only negative exponents, one per cusp class c, there is f ∈ H_k^+(Γ) whose principal part at every cusp c is Q_c + (a constant). If k < 0, f is unique (M_k(Γ) = 0 and constant principal parts force f ∈ M_k). For Γ = SL₂(ℤ) this is Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.11; the all-cusps form is the one used in Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades' proof of Corollary 4.3 ('According to Lemma 3.11 of [7]').
hypotheses: k ≠ 1; for uniqueness k < 0.
Fourier coefficients use the strict period h_c. Cusp-sum weights are w_c := widthInfty(σ_c^{−1}Γσ_c), the orbit length for Γ·{±I}; w_c = h_c at regular cusps and w_c = h_c/2 at irregular cusps.
Require the same cusp-stabilizer compatibility as Sing_k(Γ). If −I ∈ Γ and k is odd, only Q=0 is possible; raw arbitrary coefficients cannot be prescribed.
proofSteps: λ_Q(g) := Σ_c w_c Σ_{n<0} Q_c(n)b_c(−n) is a linear functional on S_{2−k}(Γ); by QM.3/bruinier-funke-duality there is h ∈ H_k^+ with {g, h} = {g, h}′ = λ_Q(g) (g cusp) for all g ∈ S_{2−k}.

Then λ_{Q − P(h)} vanishes on S_{2−k}; choose constants c_c so that the principal part Q − P(h) + c is orthogonal to λ(M_{2−k}) (the Eisenstein part of M_{2−k} is detected by constant terms), and apply QM.3/borcherds-obstruction-theorem to get h′ ∈ M^!_k with that principal part.

Uniqueness for k < 0: two solutions differ by f₀ ∈ H_k^+ with constant principal parts; {g, f₀} = Σ w_c a_c(0)b_c(0) = 0 for cusp forms, so ξf₀ = 0 and f₀ ∈ M^!_k with constant principal parts, i.e. f₀ ∈ M_k(Γ) = 0.
acceptance: Level one, k = 2 − κ with κ ≥ 4 even: the unique f with principal part q^{−m} + const is Q(−m, κ, 1) (QM.3/level-one-plus-space-spanned-by-poincare-series).

sources.match: Prescribed principal parts must respect the full stabilizer law (including the central element); the source preceding paragraph symmetrises h and −h. The scalar extraction now imposes this compatibility explicitly.
The all-cusps form used for finite-index Γ.

nodes.title: The classical Kloosterman sum K(m, n, c)
nodes.statement: For m, n ∈ ℤ and c ∈ ℕ, c ≥ 1: K(m, n, c) := Σ_{v ∈ (ℤ/cℤ)^×} e((m v̄ + n v)/c), where v v̄ ≡ 1 mod c (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (6.6)). This is the untwisted Kloosterman sum; it is not the eta-multiplier sum A_k(n) of Rademacher's formula (QM.2/kloosterman-sum-rademacher).
hypotheses: c ≥ 1; for c = 1 the sum has the single term v = 0 ∈ (ℤ/1)^× and K(m, n, 1) = 1.
proofSteps: Define as a finite sum over the units of ZMod c with the additive character e(·/c).
Symmetry K(m, n, c) = K(n, m, c) (substitute v ↦ v̄) and K(m, n, c) = K(−m, −n, c) = \overline{K(m, n, c)} (substitute v ↦ −v), so K is real.
K(m, 0, c) = K(0, m, c) is the Ramanujan sum c_c(m); K(0, 0, c) = φ(c).

sources.match: Exactly the definition.

nodes.title: Holomorphic Poincaré series P(m, k, N)
nodes.statement: For N ≥ 1, an even integer k ≥ 4 and m ∈ ℤ: P(m, k, N; τ) := Σ_{A ∈ Γ∞\Γ₀(N)} (e(mτ)|_kA)(τ), Γ∞ = {±T^n}, i.e. Σ over coprime (c, d) with N | c modulo ±1 of (cτ + d)^{−k}e(m(aτ + b)/(cτ + d)) (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (6.4), (6.5) with φ_m(y) = e(imy) = e^{−2πmy}). The series converges absolutely and locally uniformly for k ≥ 3 when m ≥ 0 and for all m (poles are only at the cusps) because |e(mAτ)| ≤ e^{2π|m|Im Aτ} and Im Aτ ≤ 1/(c²v) for c ≠ 0.
hypotheses: k even (for odd k the terms for ±A cancel), k ≥ 4 (absolute convergence; BOR treat k = 2 by analytic continuation, not planned here).
Normalisation: the identity coset contributes e(mτ).
proofSteps: Well defined on Γ∞\Γ₀(N): e(mτ)|_kT^n = e(mτ), and |_k(−I) = (−1)^k = 1.

Convergence: Σ_{(c,d)}|cτ + d|^{−k} converges locally uniformly for k ≥ 3 (Mathlib's EisensteinSeries.summable_norm_eisSummand / eisensteinSeries_tendstoLocallyUniformly), and e^{2π|m|/(c²v)} is bounded for c ≠ 0 on compacta.
Holomorphic (locally uniform limit), Γ₀(N)-invariant of weight k (re-indexing the sum).
Growth: at ∞ the identity term gives e(mτ); all other terms are O(v^{1−k}) in total; similarly at other cusps. Hence P(m) ∈ M^!_k(Γ₀(N)), a cusp form for m ≥ 1, and P(0, k, 1) = ModularForm.E k.
acceptance: P(0, k, 1) = E_k (Mathlib's ModularForm.E); P(m, k, N) ∈ S_k(Γ₀(N)) for m ≥ 1; P(−m, k, N) ∈ M^!_k(Γ₀(N)) with principal part q^{−m} at ∞.

sources.match: Exactly the definition.

nodes.title: Maass–Poincaré series Q(−m, k, N)
nodes.statement: For N ≥ 1, even k ≥ 4 and m ≥ 1: Q(−m, k, N; τ) := Σ_{A ∈ Γ∞\Γ₀(N)} (ψ_m|_{2−k}A)(τ) with seed ψ_m(τ) := P(k−1, 4πmv)·e(−mτ), where P(s, x) = γ(s, x)/Γ(s) is Tau Ceti's TauCeti.regularizedGamma. The seed is Hejhal's M-Whittaker seed of Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (6.7) in its intended normalisation: (1/(k−1)!)·M_{k/2}(−4πmv)e(−mu) with M_s(y) = |y|^{(k−2)/2}M_{(1−k/2)sgn y, s−1/2}(|y|) (DLMF 8.5.4 gives M_{(k−2)/2,(k−1)/2}(x) = (k−1)x^{1−k/2}e^{x/2}γ(k−1, x)); BOR print the weight-k normalisation, which is undefined here (sourceIssue E404). Equivalently ψ_m = e(−mτ) − Γ(k−1, 4πmv)e(−mτ)/(k−2)!, the sum of the holomorphic term q^{−m} and a decaying non-holomorphic basis function of weight 2 − k.
hypotheses: k even ≥ 4, m ≥ 1, N ≥ 1; weight of Q is 2 − k ≤ −2.
The case k = 2 (weight 0, Rademacher-type sums, needing analytic continuation) is not part of this definition.
proofSteps: Seed bounds: 0 ≤ P(k−1, x) ≤ min(1, x^{k−1}/(k−1)!) (γ(s, x) ≤ x^s/s), so |ψ_m(τ)| ≤ C min(e^{2πmv}, v^{k−1}e^{2πmv}).

For A = (a b; c d) with c ≠ 0: Im Aτ = v/|cτ + d|² ≤ 1/(c²v), so |(ψ_m|_{2−k}A)(τ)| ≤ C′v^{k−1}|cτ + d|^{−k} on compacta; the series converges absolutely and locally uniformly (k ≥ 3), with its derivatives.
Well defined on Γ∞\Γ₀(N): ψ_m(τ + 1) = ψ_m(τ) and weight 2 − k even.
acceptance: The identity term of Q(−m, k, N) is q^{−m} − Γ(k−1, 4πmv)q^{−m}/(k−2)!, matching the leading terms q^{−m} of Q⁺ and −Γ(k−1, 4πmy)q^{−m}/(k−2)! of Q⁻ in BOR Prop. 6.2.
For N = 1, m = 1, k = 12: the constant term of the holomorphic part is −65520/691 ≈ −94.8191 (BOR Prop. 6.2; numerically confirmed), and a⁺(1) ≈ −1842.89472.

sources.match: The definition as printed (with the weight slip E404).

nodes.title: Q(−m, k, N) is a harmonic Maass form in H_{2−k}^+
nodes.statement: For N ≥ 1, even k ≥ 4, m ≥ 1: Q(−m, k, N) ∈ H_{2−k}^+(Γ₀(N)); its principal part at ∞ is q^{−m} + a constant, and at every cusp of Γ₀(N) inequivalent to ∞ its principal part is constant (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Prop. 6.2, first assertion).
hypotheses: As in QM.3/maass-poincare-series.
proofSteps: Harmonic: Δ_{2−k}ψ_m = 0 (holomorphic term plus the decaying basis function, QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying) and Δ commutes with the slash (QM.3/laplacian-slash-equivariance); the series converges with two derivatives locally uniformly.
Invariance: re-indexing over Γ∞\Γ₀(N); C²: locally uniform convergence of derivatives.

Growth at ∞: Q − ψ_m = O(v^{k−1}·v^{1−k}) = O(1) (sum over c ≠ 0 of v^{k−1}|cτ + d|^{−k} is O(v^{1−k}) times v^{k−1}), so Q − q^{−m} is bounded; at a cusp σ∞ not equivalent to ∞ no term is fixed and (Q|σ) is bounded.

Hence exponential growth everywhere, and after removing q^{−m} (at ∞) Q is bounded at the cusps, so by QM.3/plus-space-principal-part-characterisation (with the boundedness implying the non-holomorphic terms decay) Q ∈ H_{2−k}^+.
acceptance: For N = 1 the principal part is q^{−m} + a⁺(0).

sources.match: The membership (BOR's H_{2−k} = H^+_{2−k}).
Same membership in the vector-valued setting.

nodes.title: ξ_{2−k}Q(−m, k, N) = (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!·P(m, k, N)
nodes.statement: For N ≥ 1, even k ≥ 4, m ≥ 1: ξ_{2−k}(Q(−m, k, N)) = ((4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!)·P(m, k, N) (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades §6.2).
hypotheses: As in QM.3/maass-poincare-series.
proofSteps: ξ_{2−k}ψ_m = 0 − ξ_{2−k}(Γ(k−1, 4πmv)e(−mτ))/(k−2)! = (4πm)^{k−1}e(mτ)/(k−2)! (QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying with w = 2 − k, n = −m, h = 1; conjugation leaves the real constant unchanged).
ξ_{2−k}(ψ_m|_{2−k}A) = (ξ_{2−k}ψ_m)|_kA (QM.3/xi-slash-equivariance), and ξ commutes with the locally uniformly convergent sum (with derivatives).
Summing over Γ∞\Γ₀(N) gives (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!·P(m, k, N).
acceptance: Consistent with QM.3/xi-fourier-expansion: a⁻(−m) = −1/(k−2)! gives leading coefficient (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!.
BOR's display: ξ_{2−k}(Q(−m, k, N; z)) = (4π)^{k−1}m^{k−1}/(k−2)!·P(m, k, N; z).

sources.match: Exactly the statement (BOR derive it from (1.3) and the expansions; here it is proved termwise).

nodes.title: The vertical-line integral for J_ν
nodes.statement: For real x > 0, real c > 0 and ν ∈ ℂ with Re ν > 0: J_ν(x) = (x/2)^ν·(1/(2π))∫_{−∞}^{∞}(c + iy)^{−ν−1}exp(c + iy − x²/(4(c + iy)))dy, i.e. J_ν(x) = (x/2)^ν(1/(2πi))∫_{c−i∞}^{c+i∞}t^{−ν−1}exp(t − x²/(4t))dt, the integral converging absolutely (t^{−ν−1} the principal power). This is the vertical-line form of Schläfli's loop integral (DLMF 10.9.19) and the J-analogue of QM.2/modified-bessel-i-bromwich-integral.
proofSteps: Expand exp(−x²/(4t)) = Σ_j (−x²/4)^j t^{−j}/j!.
On Re t = c: |t^{−ν−1−j}| ≤ e^{π|Im ν|/2}|t|^{−Re ν−1}c^{−j} and |e^t| = e^c, so Σ_j ∫|term|dy ≤ e^{c + π|Im ν|/2 + x²/(4c)}∫|c + iy|^{−Re ν−1}dy < ∞ (Re ν > 0); exchange sum and integral.
Each term: (1/(2π))∫(c + iy)^{−(ν+1+j)}e^{c+iy}dy = 1/Γ(ν + j + 1) by QM.2/bromwich-integral-reciprocal-gamma (Re(ν + 1 + j) > 1).
Sum: (x/2)^ν Σ_j(−1)^j(x²/4)^j/(j!Γ(ν + j + 1)) = J_ν(x) (QM.2/bessel-function-j).
acceptance: Replacing x by ix formally turns it into QM.2/modified-bessel-i-bromwich-integral.
ν = 1/2: both sides equal √(2/(πx))·sin x.

sources.match: Schläfli's loop integral; for Re ν > 0 the loop around the negative axis may be opened to the vertical line Re t = c (the integrand is O(|t|^{−Re ν−1}) there), which is the form stated.

nodes.title: Fourier coefficients of holomorphic Poincaré series
nodes.statement: For even k ≥ 4 and m, N ≥ 1: P(m, k, N) = q^m + Σ_{n≥1} a(m, k, N; n)q^n with a(m, k, N; n) = 2π(−1)^{k/2}(n/m)^{(k−1)/2} Σ_{c>0, N|c} K(m, n, c)/c · J_{k−1}(4π√(mn)/c) for n ≥ 1 (the q^m term included in the n = m term by the Kronecker delta convention of BOR (6.5)); and P(−m, k, N) = q^{−m} + Σ_{n≥1} a(−m, k, N; n)q^n with a(−m, k, N; n) = 2π(−1)^{k/2}(n/m)^{(k−1)/2}Σ_{c>0, N|c} K(−m, n, c)/c · I_{k−1}(4π√(mn)/c) (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Prop. 6.1).
hypotheses: k even ≥ 4, m ≥ 1, N ≥ 1; J_ν = QM.2/bessel-function-j, I_ν = QM.2/modified-bessel-function-i; a(±m, k, N; n) real.
proofSteps: Split the sum over Γ∞\Γ₀(N) into the class of I (the term q^{±m}) and the classes with c > 0, N | c; the latter are A = (a b; c d) with d running over integers prime to c, and for fixed c and d mod c the sum over the translates d + jc (j ∈ ℤ) is F_{c,d}(τ) = Σ_j f_c(τ + d/c + j) with f_c(τ) = (cτ)^{−k}e(±m(a/c − 1/(c²τ))).

F_{c,d} is holomorphic and 1-periodic; its n-th Fourier coefficient is ∫_0^1 F_{c,d}(x + iy)e(−n(x + iy))dx = e(±ma/c + nd/c)∫_ℝ f̃_c(x + iy)e(−n(x + iy))dx with f̃_c(τ) = (cτ)^{−k}e(∓m/(c²τ)) (unfolding; Fubini is justified by absolute convergence, k ≥ 4). Summing over d mod c prime to c gives K(±m, n, c) (QM.3/classical-kloosterman-sum; ad ≡ 1 mod c).

For n ≤ 0 the integral vanishes: it does not depend on y (Cauchy's theorem; the integrand is holomorphic and O(|τ|^{−k})), and it is O(y^{1−k}) as y → ∞ because |e(−nτ)| ≤ 1 and e(∓m/(c²τ)) is bounded for y ≥ 1.

For n ≥ 1 substitute t = −2πinτ (τ = it/(2πn)), which maps the line Im τ = y onto Re t = 2πny traversed downwards, with (cτ)^{−k} = c^{−k}(2πn)^k(−1)^{k/2}t^{−k} (k even) and dx = (i/(2πn))dt: ∫_ℝ(cτ)^{−k}e(∓m/(c²τ))e(−nτ)dx = c^{−k}(2πn)^{k−1}(−1)^{k/2}·2π·(1/(2πi))∫_{2πny−i∞}^{2πny+i∞}t^{−k}exp(t ∓ 4π²mn/(c²t))dt.

With ν = k − 1 and x = 4π√(mn)/c (x²/4 = 4π²mn/c²) the last factor is (x/2)^{−ν}J_ν(x) for P(m, k, N) (sign −; QM.3/bessel-j-bromwich-integral) and (x/2)^{−ν}I_ν(x) for P(−m, k, N) (sign +; QM.2/modified-bessel-i-bromwich-integral). Since (x/2)^{−(k−1)} = (c/(2π√(mn)))^{k−1}, the constants collect to 2π(−1)^{k/2}(n/m)^{(k−1)/2}/c.

Absolute convergence of the c-sum: |K(±m, n, c)| ≤ c and |J_{k−1}(x)|, |I_{k−1}(x)| ≤ C x^{k−1} for 0 < x ≤ 4π√(mn), so the c-term is O(c^{1−k}); and F = Σ_c Σ_d F_{c,d} converges locally uniformly (QM.3/holomorphic-poincare-series), so its Fourier coefficients are the sums of those of the F_{c,d}.
acceptance: For N = 1, k = 12, m = 1: P(1, 12, 1) is a non-zero multiple of Δ, so a(1, 12, 1; n)/(1 + a(1, 12, 1; 1)) = τ(n) (checked numerically: truncating the c-sum at c < 4000 gives a(1, 12, 1; 1) ≈ 1.84029, a(2)/(1 + a(1)) = −24.000, a(3)/(1 + a(1)) = 252.000).
m = 0 is excluded: then P(0, k, N) is the Eisenstein series at ∞, whose coefficients are divisor sums, not Bessel sums.

sources.match: Part 1; part 2 is the same with K(−m, n, c) and I_{k−1}. BOR give no proof ('well known (for example, see [11, 15])').

nodes.title: Fourier expansion of Maass–Poincaré series
hypotheses: As in QM.3/maass-poincare-series. Here b(n) denotes the Bessel-sum correction after the seed is written separately: the total non-holomorphic coefficient at n<0 is −δ_{n,−m}/(k−2)! + b(n). The holomorphic q^{−m} seed is also separate.
proofSteps: Shape: Q ∈ H_{2−k}^+(Γ₀(N)) with principal part q^{−m} + const at ∞ (QM.3/maass-poincare-series-harmonic), so Q = Σ_{n≫−∞}b⁺(n)q^n + Σ_{n<0}b(n)Γ(k−1, 4π|n|v)q^n (QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion; the v^{k−1} term is absent because ξ_{2−k}Q is a cusp form).

Non-holomorphic coefficients (n < 0): ξ_{2−k}Q = ((4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!)·P(m, k, N) (QM.3/xi-maass-poincare-series), and ξ_{2−k}(b(n)Γ(k−1, 4π|n|v)q^n) = −\overline{b(n)}(4π|n|)^{k−1}q^{|n|} (QM.3/xi-fourier-expansion). Comparing coefficients of q^{|n|} with QM.3/holomorphic-poincare-series-fourier-expansion (coefficients real; K(−m, n, c) = K(m, |n|, c) for n < 0) gives −δ_{n,−m}/(k−2)! + b(n) = −(m/|n|)^{k−1}(δ_{|n|,m} + a(m, k, N; |n|))/(k−2)!, which is the stated J-Bessel formula (the Kronecker-delta terms agree and cancel, leaving b(n) as the correction only).

Holomorphic coefficients (n > 0): D^{k−1}Q = −m^{k−1}P(−m, k, N) (QM.3/bol-image-of-maass-poincare-series) and D^{k−1}Q = Σ b⁺(n)n^{k−1}q^n (QM.3/flipping-derivative-theorem); comparing with the I-Bessel expansion of P(−m, k, N) gives b⁺(n) = −(m/n)^{k−1}a(−m, k, N; n), the stated formula.

Constant term: b⁺(0) = ∫_0^1 Q(x + iy)dx for every y (the only y-independent zeroth-mode term). Unfold as in the holomorphic case: the class of I contributes 0 (ψ_m has only the mode −m), and the class (c, d mod c) contributes e(−ma/c)·∫_ℝ(cτ)^{k−2}ψ_m(−1/(c²τ))dx (ψ_m(τ + r) = e(−mr)ψ_m(τ) for real r, ad ≡ 1 mod c), whose d-sum gives K(−m, 0, c).

Since b⁺(0) does not depend on y, let y → ∞: substituting x = yt, Im(−1/(c²τ)) = 1/(c²y(1 + t²)) → 0 and P(k−1, X) = X^{k−1}/(k−1)! + O(X^k), so the c-term tends to ((4πm)^{k−1}/((k−1)!c^k))∫_ℝ dt/((t + i)(t − i)^{k−1}) = ((4πm)^{k−1}/((k−1)!c^k))·(−2π(−1)^{k/2}/2^{k−1}) (residue at t = −i), by dominated convergence (integrand O((1 + t²)^{−k/2})). Summing over c (|K(−m, 0, c)| ≤ c, k ≥ 4) gives b⁺(0) = −(2π)^k(−1)^{k/2}m^{k−1}/(k−1)!·Σ_{c>0, N|c}K(−m, 0, c)/c^k.
acceptance: N = 1, m = 1, k = 12: b(0) = −(2π)^{12}/(11!·ζ(12)) = −65520/691 (since K(−1, 0, c) = μ(c) and Σ_c μ(c)c^{−12} = 1/ζ(12)), b(1) ≈ −1842.89472, b(2) ≈ −23274.07545, b(3) ≈ −225028.75877 (numerically checked; these agree with BOR's list except its constant term, E405).

Consistency with QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing-formula at level one: {E_k, Q(−m, k, 1)} = 0 gives b⁺(0) = (2k/B_k)σ_{k−1}(m), which equals the Kloosterman-sum formula because Σ_c K(−m, 0, c)c^{−k} = σ_{1−k}(m)/ζ(k) (Ramanujan sums).

nodes.title: H_{2−k}^+(SL₂(ℤ)) is spanned by Maass–Poincaré series
nodes.statement: For even k ≥ 4: every f ∈ H_{2−k}^+(SL₂(ℤ)) is a finite linear combination Σ_{m=1}^{M} a⁺(−m)·Q(−m, k, 1) of Maass–Poincaré series (a⁺ its holomorphic coefficients). In particular f is determined by its principal part without constant term, and M^!_{2−k}(SL₂(ℤ)) ⊆ span{Q(−m, k, 1)} (Bruinier–Funke Remark 3.10, scalar level one).
hypotheses: Level one; weight 2 − k ≤ −2.
proofSteps: g := f − Σ_{m=1}^{M} a⁺(−m)Q(−m, k, 1) ∈ H_{2−k}^+ has principal part a constant c₀ (QM.3/maass-poincare-series-harmonic).
For every cusp form h ∈ S_k(SL₂(ℤ)): {h, g} = c₀·b_h(0) = 0 (QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing-formula), so (h, ξg) = 0 for all h, hence ξg = 0 (take h = ξg; positivity).
So g ∈ M^!_{2−k}(SL₂(ℤ)) with constant principal part, i.e. g ∈ M_{2−k}(SL₂(ℤ)) = 0 (negative weight; Mathlib ModularFormClass.levelOne_neg_weight_eq_zero).

sources.match: The spanning statement (proof cited to Bruinier's Lecture Notes, not public; the proof steps here use only BF §3).
Principal parts of the Poincaré series (scalar: q^{−m} + constant).

nodes.title: S_k(SL₂(ℤ)) is spanned by holomorphic Poincaré series
nodes.statement: For even k ≥ 4, S_k(SL₂(ℤ)) is spanned by {P(m, k, 1) : m ≥ 1}.
hypotheses: Level one, k even ≥ 4.
proofSteps: By QM.3/bruinier-funke-exact-sequences, ξ_{2−k} maps H_{2−k}^+(SL₂(ℤ)) onto S_k(SL₂(ℤ)).

By QM.3/level-one-plus-space-spanned-by-poincare-series every element of H_{2−k}^+ is a combination of Q(−m, k, 1), and ξ_{2−k}Q(−m, k, 1) = (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!·P(m, k, 1) (QM.3/xi-maass-poincare-series); ξ is conjugate-linear, so the images span.

nodes.title: D^{k−1} maps H_{2−k}^+ to weakly holomorphic forms (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Theorem 1.1)
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, k ≥ 2 an integer and f ∈ H_{2−k}^+(Γ). Then D^{k−1}f ∈ M^!_k(Γ) (D = (2πi)^{−1}∂_τ), and at ∞ (width h) D^{k−1}f = D^{k−1}f⁺ = Σ_{n≫−∞} a⁺(n)(n/h)^{k−1}e(nτ/h); for h = 1 this is Σ a⁺(n)n^{k−1}q^n.
hypotheses: k ≥ 2; BOR state it for Γ₀(N) with character; the proof is the same for finite-index Γ.
proofSteps: Bol (QM.3/bol-identity): D^{k−1}f = (−4π)^{1−k}R^{k−1}_{2−k}f, so D^{k−1}f has the weight-k transformation law (iteratedRaising_slash).

Holomorphy: from Δ_{2−k}f = 0 and QM.3/raising-lowering-eigenvalue-shift by induction Δ_{k−2}R^{k−2}_{2−k}f = (2 − k)R^{k−2}_{2−k}f; then L_kR^{k−1}_{2−k}f = (L_kR_{k−2})R^{k−2}_{2−k}f = (−Δ_{k−2} − (k − 2))R^{k−2}_{2−k}f = 0 (QM.3/laplacian-raising-lowering-factorisation), and L_k = 0 means holomorphic.

Expansion: for n<0, Γ(k−1,4π|n|v/h)e(nτ/h) is (k−2)!e(nτ̄/h) times a polynomial in v of degree k−2 (upperIncompleteGamma_nat_add_one). D differentiates v and kills e(nτ̄/h), so D^{k−1} kills this basis function. Apply termwise on compacta using the coefficient bounds and derivative-series convergence; D^{k−1}e(nτ/h)=(n/h)^{k−1}e(nτ/h). Holomorphy and decay alone would not imply vanishing.
Meromorphic at the cusps: finitely many negative n.
acceptance: For f = Q(−m, k, N): D^{k−1}Q = −m^{k−1}P(−m, k, N) (QM.3/bol-image-of-maass-poincare-series).
For f ∈ M^!_{2−k}: the classical fact that D^{k−1} maps M^!_{2−k} to M^!_k.

sources.match: Exactly the statement (BOR's H is our H^+).
The holomorphy step.

nodes.title: D^{k−1}Q(−m, k, N) = −m^{k−1}P(−m, k, N)
nodes.statement: For even k ≥ 4 and m, N ≥ 1: D^{k−1}Q(−m, k, N) = −m^{k−1}·P(−m, k, N) (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (6.8)).

proofSteps: D^{k−1}ψ_m = D^{k−1}(q^{−m}) − 0 = (−m)^{k−1}q^{−m} = −m^{k−1}q^{−m} (k even; D^{k−1} kills the non-holomorphic basis function by QM.3/flipping-derivative-theorem's proof).
D^{k−1}(ψ_m|_{2−k}A) = (D^{k−1}ψ_m)|_kA by QM.3/bol-identity; sum over Γ∞\Γ₀(N) with the locally uniform convergence of derivatives.

nodes.title: The truncated (regularized) Petersson product
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index and k ∈ ℤ. For g ∈ M_k(Γ) and h ∈ M^!_k(Γ) with vanishing constant term at every cusp: (g, h)^{reg} := [SL₂(ℤ) : Γ]^{−1}·lim_{T→∞} ∫_{F_T(Γ)} g(τ)\overline{h(τ)}v^k dμ, where F_T(Γ) is the union of γF_T over effective cosets (Γ⟨−I⟩)\SL₂(ℤ), taking one copy of each geometric fundamental-domain piece and F_T is the truncated standard fundamental domain. This is Borcherds' regularization (constant term at s = 0 of the continuation in s) in the case where no continuation is needed (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades §4, Remark 8); it reduces to the normalised Petersson product for cusp forms.
hypotheses: h has vanishing constant term at every cusp (otherwise the limit need not exist and Borcherds' meromorphic continuation in s is required; that general regularization is not planned here).
Normalisation: divided by the index [SL₂(ℤ) : Γ] (BOR), unlike QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing.

Keep the full index [SL₂(ℤ):Γ] in the denominator and use effective cosets modulo Γ⟨−I⟩ in the domain, as in the pinned Tau Ceti Petersson integral. For −I ∉ Γ this convention contributes half the full-coset-sum normalization. BOR treat Γ₀(N), which contains −I, so their convention agrees there.
proofSteps: Existence of the limit: on each cusp region the integrand is Σ_{n}b_g(n)\overline{a_h(n)}e^{−4πnv/h}v^{k−2} after integrating in u; the only possibly divergent terms are those with n ≤ 0, which vanish because a_h(0) = 0 and b_g(n) = 0 for n < 0.
Compatibility: for h a cusp form the limit is the absolutely convergent integral.
acceptance: For g, h ∈ S_k(Γ): (g, h)^{reg} = [SL₂(ℤ) : Γ]^{−1}·Tau Ceti's CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets h g (the same integral; Tau Ceti is conjugate-linear in h and linear in g).
